```{r}
# ============================================================================
# STUDY AREA MAP USING EXISTING POLAR PROJECTION FRAMEWORK
# ============================================================================

# --- SETUP ---
plot_dir <- here("Plots", "introduction")
if (!dir.exists(plot_dir)) dir.create(plot_dir, recursive = TRUE)

cat("\n", rep("=", 80), "\n")
cat("CREATING STUDY AREA MAP (POLAR PROJECTION)\n")
cat(rep("=", 80), "\n\n")

# ============================================================================z
# DEFINE PROJECTION (same as your existing code)
# ============================================================================

arctic_crs <- "+proj=laea +lat_0=90 +lon_0=0"

# ============================================================================
# CREATE STUDY REGION POLYGONS
# ============================================================================

# Fram Strait: 15°W to 15°E, 76°N to 82°N
fram_coords <- matrix(c(
  -15, 76,
  15, 76,
  15, 82,
  -15, 82,
  -15, 76
), ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)

fram_polygon <- st_polygon(list(fram_coords)) %>%
  st_sfc(crs = 4326) %>%
  st_sf(region = "Fram Strait")

# Svalbard-Barents: 10°W to 35°E, 74°N to 81°N
svalbard_coords <- matrix(c(
  -10, 74,
  35, 74,
  35, 81,
  -10, 81,
  -10, 74
), ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)

svalbard_polygon <- st_polygon(list(svalbard_coords)) %>%
  st_sfc(crs = 4326) %>%
  st_sf(region = "Svalbard-Barents")

# Combine and transform to polar projection
study_regions <- rbind(fram_polygon, svalbard_polygon)
study_regions_polar <- st_transform(study_regions, crs = arctic_crs)

# ============================================================================
# LOAD AND TRANSFORM BASE MAP DATA
# ============================================================================

world <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")
world_polar <- st_transform(world, crs = arctic_crs)

# ============================================================================
# CREATE CARTOGRAPHIC ELEMENTS (same as your existing code)
# ============================================================================

view_radius <- 3700000
plot_radius <- 4400000

# Circular mask
circle_mask <- st_sfc(st_point(c(0, 0)), crs = arctic_crs) %>%
  st_buffer(dist = view_radius)

# Inverse mask for corners
square_box <- st_as_sfc(st_bbox(c(
  xmin = -plot_radius, xmax = plot_radius,
  ymin = -plot_radius, ymax = plot_radius
), crs = arctic_crs))
inverse_mask <- st_difference(square_box, circle_mask)

# Graticules
graticules <- st_graticule(
  lon = seq(-180, 180, by = 60),
  lat = c(60, 70, 80),
  crs = 4326
) %>%
  st_transform(crs = arctic_crs)

# Latitude labels
lat_labels <- data.frame(
  lon = 180,
  lat = c(60, 70, 80)
) %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) %>%
  st_transform(crs = arctic_crs)
lat_labels$label <- c("60°N", "70°N", "80°N")

# Longitude labels
lon_labels <- data.frame(
  lon = seq(0, 300, by = 60),
  lat = 54
) %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) %>%
  st_transform(crs = arctic_crs)
lon_labels$label <- c("0°", "60°E", "120°E", "180°", "120°W", "60°W")

# ============================================================================
# CREATE THE MAP
# ============================================================================

p_study <- ggplot() +
  
  # 1. Ocean background
  geom_sf(data = circle_mask, fill = "#B8D4E8", color = NA) +
  
  # 2. Graticules
 geom_sf(data = graticules, color = "gray50", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.25) +
  
  # 3. Land masses
  geom_sf(data = world_polar, fill = "#E8DCC8", color = "gray30", linewidth = 0.3) +
  
  # 4. Study regions - Svalbard-Barents (blue, behind)
  geom_sf(data = study_regions_polar[study_regions_polar$region == "Svalbard-Barents", ],
          fill = "#2196F3", color = "#0D47A1", alpha = 0.4, linewidth = 1.2) +
  
  # 5. Study regions - Fram Strait (orange, on top)
  geom_sf(data = study_regions_polar[study_regions_polar$region == "Fram Strait", ],
          fill = "#FF9800", color = "#E65100", alpha = 0.5, linewidth = 1.2) +
  
  # 6. Inverse mask (white corners)
  geom_sf(data = inverse_mask, fill = "white", color = NA) +
  
  # 7. Labels
  geom_sf_text(data = lat_labels, aes(label = label), size = 2.5, color = "black", hjust = 1.2) +
  geom_sf_text(data = lon_labels, aes(label = label), size = 2.5, color = "black") +
  
  # 8. Set coordinates
 coord_sf(xlim = c(-plot_radius, plot_radius), 
           ylim = c(-plot_radius, plot_radius), 
           expand = FALSE) +
  
  # 9. Title and theme
  labs(
    title = "Study Regions for Arctic Storminess Analysis",
    subtitle = "Fram Strait (orange): 15°W–15°E, 76°N–82°N | Svalbard-Barents (blue): 10°W–35°E, 74°N–81°N"
  ) +
  
  theme_void(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = 16),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10, color = "gray30"),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "gray95", color = NA),
    plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10)
  )

# Save
output_file <- file.path(plot_dir, "Fig_Study_Area_Polar.png")
ggsave(output_file, p_study, width = 10, height = 10, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
cat(sprintf("  ✓ Saved: %s\n", basename(output_file)))

cat("\n", rep("=", 80), "\n")
cat("STUDY AREA MAP COMPLETE!\n")
cat(rep("=", 80), "\n")
```

# Pan Arctic

## Phase 1

```{r summary}
# ============================================================================
# PHASE 1: DATA QUALITY CONTROL & VALIDATION VISUALIZATIONS
#
# PURPOSE: Create diagnostic plots demonstrating:
#   1. Data completeness and coverage (1958-2024)
#   2. Spatial domain and regional mask verification
#   3. Reynolds decomposition validation (MKE + EKE checks)
#   4. Climatological patterns (sanity checks)
#   5. Seasonal cycle verification
#
# OUTPUTS: Publication-quality figures for Methods section
# ============================================================================

# --- SETUP ---
processed_dir <- "E:/ERA5_data/processed"
plot_dir <- file.path(processed_dir, "phase1_diagnostics")
if (!dir.exists(plot_dir)) dir.create(plot_dir, recursive = TRUE)

# ============================================================================
# PLOT 1: SPATIAL DOMAIN MAP WITH REGIONAL MASKS
# ============================================================================

cat("\nGenerating Plot 1: Spatial Domain and Regional Masks...\n")

# Load one file to get coordinates
nc <- nc_open(file.path(processed_dir, "ERA5_MKE_monthly_1958-2024.nc"))
lat <- ncvar_get(nc, "latitude")
lon <- ncvar_get(nc, "longitude")
nc_close(nc)

# Get world map
world <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")

# Create data frame for Arctic domain
arctic_domain <- expand.grid(lon = lon, lat = lat) %>%
  filter(lat >= 60)

# Define regions as polygons
regions <- list(
  Pan_Arctic = data.frame(
    lon = c(-180, 180, 180, -180, -180),
    lat = c(60, 60, 90, 90, 60),
    region = "Pan-Arctic (≥60°N)"
  ),
  Fram_Strait = data.frame(
    lon = c(-15, 15, 15, -15, -15),
    lat = c(76, 76, 82, 82, 76),
    region = "Fram Strait"
  ),
  Svalbard_Barents = data.frame(
    lon = c(-10, 35, 35, -10, -10),
    lat = c(74, 74, 81, 81, 74),
    region = "Svalbard/Barents"
  )
)

region_df <- bind_rows(regions)

p1 <- ggplot() +
  # World background
  geom_sf(data = world, fill = "gray90", color = "gray60", linewidth = 0.3) +
  # Data coverage
  geom_tile(data = arctic_domain, aes(x = lon, y = lat), 
            fill = "#E3F2FD", alpha = 0.6) +
  # Regional masks
  geom_polygon(data = region_df, 
               aes(x = lon, y = lat, color = region, fill = region),
               alpha = 0.2, linewidth = 1.5) +
  # Arctic Circle
  geom_hline(yintercept = 66.5, linetype = "dashed", 
             color = "red", linewidth = 0.8, alpha = 0.7) +
  annotate("text", x = -170, y = 67.5, label = "Arctic Circle (66.5°N)", 
           color = "red", size = 3.5, fontface = "italic") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#1E88E5", "#D32F2F", "#7B1FA2"),
                     name = "Analysis Regions") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#1E88E5", "#D32F2F", "#7B1FA2"),
                    name = "Analysis Regions") +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-180, 180), ylim = c(55, 90), 
           crs = "+proj=stere +lat_0=90") +
  labs(
    title = "Arctic Analysis Domain and Regional Masks",
    subtitle = "ERA5 Data Coverage: 1958-2024 | 0.25° × 0.25° Resolution",
    x = "Longitude",
    y = "Latitude"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = 16),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 12),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid = element_line(color = "gray80", linewidth = 0.3)
  )

ggsave(file.path(plot_dir, "Fig1_Spatial_Domain.png"), 
       plot = p1, width = 12, height = 10, dpi = 300)

cat("  ✓ Saved: Fig1_Spatial_Domain.png\n")

# ============================================================================
# PLOT 2: TEMPORAL COVERAGE AND DATA COMPLETENESS
# ============================================================================

cat("\nGenerating Plot 2: Temporal Coverage...\n")

# Load MKE data to check completeness
nc <- nc_open(file.path(processed_dir, "ERA5_MKE_monthly_1958-2024.nc"))
mke <- ncvar_get(nc, "mke")
time_var <- ncvar_get(nc, "time")
nc_close(nc)

# Create time series of data availability
# mke has dimensions [lon, lat, time], so time is 3rd dimension
n_times <- dim(mke)[3]  # Correct: time dimension
cat(sprintf("  Time dimension size: %d months\n", n_times))
dates <- seq(as.Date("1958-01-01"), by = "month", length.out = n_times)

# Calculate completeness for each time step
# mke dimensions: [360 lon, 35 lat, 804 time]
cat("  Calculating data completeness...")
completeness <- data.frame(
  date = dates,
  year = year(dates),
  month = month(dates, label = TRUE),
  n_valid = numeric(n_times),
  n_total = dim(mke)[1] * dim(mke)[2]  # lon * lat
)

# Loop over time dimension (3rd dimension)
progress_interval <- max(1, floor(n_times / 10))
for (i in 1:n_times) {
  if (i %% progress_interval == 0) {
    cat(sprintf(" %d%%", round(100 * i / n_times)))
  }
  completeness$n_valid[i] <- sum(!is.na(mke[, , i]))
}

completeness <- completeness %>%
  mutate(
    pct_complete = (n_valid / n_total) * 100,
    is_complete = pct_complete > 99
  )

cat(" Done!\n")

# Free up memory (we'll reload for next section)
rm(mke)
gc(verbose = FALSE)

# Panel A: Timeline
panel_a <- ggplot(completeness, aes(x = date, y = pct_complete)) +
  geom_line(color = "#1E88E5", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(color = is_complete), size = 1, alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "#4CAF50", "FALSE" = "#D32F2F"),
                     name = "Complete", guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(95, 100), breaks = seq(95, 100, 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "A) Temporal Coverage",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Data Completeness (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

# Panel B: Monthly distribution
panel_b <- completeness %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarize(
    mean_complete = mean(pct_complete),
    n_months = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = month, y = mean_complete)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#1E88E5", alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 100, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(95, 100)) +
  labs(
    title = "B) By Month",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Mean Completeness (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# Panel C: Yearly summary
panel_c <- completeness %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarize(
    mean_complete = mean(pct_complete),
    min_complete = min(pct_complete),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = mean_complete)) +
  geom_line(color = "#1E88E5", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "#1E88E5", size = 2) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = min_complete, ymax = mean_complete), 
              fill = "#1E88E5", alpha = 0.2) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(95, 100)) +
  labs(
    title = "C) By Year",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Mean Completeness (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

p2 <- panel_a / (panel_b | panel_c) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Data Completeness Assessment: ERA5 Arctic Domain (1958-2024)",
    subtitle = sprintf("Total: %d months | Mean completeness: %.2f%%", 
                      nrow(completeness), mean(completeness$pct_complete)),
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5)
    )
  )

ggsave(file.path(plot_dir, "Fig2_Temporal_Coverage.png"), 
       plot = p2, width = 14, height = 10, dpi = 300)

cat("  ✓ Saved: Fig2_Temporal_Coverage.png\n")

# ============================================================================
# PLOT 3: REYNOLDS DECOMPOSITION VALIDATION
# ============================================================================

cat("\nGenerating Plot 3: Reynolds Decomposition Validation...\n")

# Load MKE and EKE for validation
nc_mke <- nc_open(file.path(processed_dir, "ERA5_MKE_monthly_1958-2024.nc"))
nc_eke <- nc_open(file.path(processed_dir, "ERA5_EKE_monthly_1958-2024.nc"))

mke <- ncvar_get(nc_mke, "mke")
eke <- ncvar_get(nc_eke, "eke")

nc_close(nc_mke)
nc_close(nc_eke)

# Calculate area-weighted Pan-Arctic means
# NetCDF structure shows: mke[longitude, latitude, time]
# So when loaded, mke has dimensions: [360 lon, 35 lat, 804 time]

# Calculate area-weighted Pan-Arctic means
# NetCDF structure shows: mke[longitude, latitude, time]
# So when loaded, mke has dimensions: [360 lon, 35 lat, 804 time]

cat(sprintf("  Original dimensions: [%s]\n", paste(dim(mke), collapse = " × ")))
cat(sprintf("  Original order: [longitude=%d, latitude=%d, time=%d]\n", 
            dim(mke)[1], dim(mke)[2], dim(mke)[3]))

# Permute from [lon, lat, time] to [time, lat, lon]
mke_permuted <- aperm(mke, c(3, 2, 1))  # Move time to first position
eke_permuted <- aperm(eke, c(3, 2, 1))

cat(sprintf("  Permuted to: [time=%d, lat=%d, lon=%d]\n", 
            dim(mke_permuted)[1], dim(mke_permuted)[2], dim(mke_permuted)[3]))
cat(sprintf("  Number of latitudes: %d, Number of longitudes: %d\n", 
            length(lat), length(lon)))

# Verify dimensions match
if (dim(mke_permuted)[2] != length(lat) || dim(mke_permuted)[3] != length(lon)) {
  stop("Dimension mismatch after permutation!")
}

# Create latitude weights (cosine weighting for area)
lat_weights <- cos(lat * pi / 180)

# Calculate time series
cat("  Calculating area-weighted time series...")
mke_ts <- numeric(dim(mke_permuted)[1])
eke_ts <- numeric(dim(eke_permuted)[1])

n_timesteps <- dim(mke_permuted)[1]
progress_interval <- max(1, floor(n_timesteps / 10))  # Show progress every 10%

for (i in 1:n_timesteps) {
  # Show progress
  if (i %% progress_interval == 0) {
    cat(sprintf(" %d%%", round(100 * i / n_timesteps)))
  }
  
  # Extract slice [lat, lon] for this time step
  mke_slice <- mke_permuted[i, , ]  # Results in [35 lat, 360 lon]
  eke_slice <- eke_permuted[i, , ]
  
  # Create weight matrix [lat, lon] to match slice dimensions
  weights_matrix <- matrix(lat_weights, 
                           nrow = length(lat),      # 35 rows (lat)
                           ncol = length(lon),      # 360 columns (lon)
                           byrow = FALSE)
  
  # Calculate weighted mean (both now have same dimensions)
  mke_ts[i] <- weighted.mean(as.vector(mke_slice), 
                             as.vector(weights_matrix), 
                             na.rm = TRUE)
  eke_ts[i] <- weighted.mean(as.vector(eke_slice), 
                             as.vector(weights_matrix), 
                             na.rm = TRUE)
}

cat(" Done!\n")

total_ke <- mke_ts + eke_ts

# Create validation dataframe
validation_df <- data.frame(
  date = dates,
  MKE = mke_ts,
  EKE = eke_ts,
  Total = total_ke
) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(MKE, EKE), names_to = "Component", values_to = "Value")

# Panel A: Time series
panel_a <- ggplot(validation_df, aes(x = date, y = Value, color = Component)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("MKE" = "#1E88E5", "EKE" = "#D32F2F")) +
  labs(
    title = "A) MKE and EKE Time Series",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Kinetic Energy (m²/s²)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "top")

# Panel B: MKE/EKE ratio
panel_b <- data.frame(date = dates, ratio = mke_ts / eke_ts) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = date, y = ratio)) +
  geom_line(color = "#7B1FA2", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", color = "red", linewidth = 1, se = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "B) MKE/EKE Ratio",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Ratio (dimensionless)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

# Panel C: Scatter plot
panel_c <- data.frame(MKE = mke_ts, EKE = eke_ts) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = EKE, y = MKE)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, color = "#1E88E5", size = 2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red", linewidth = 1, se = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "C) MKE vs EKE Relationship",
    x = "EKE (m²/s²)",
    y = "MKE (m²/s²)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

# Panel D: Component proportions
panel_d <- data.frame(
  date = dates,
  MKE_pct = (mke_ts / total_ke) * 100,
  EKE_pct = (eke_ts / total_ke) * 100
) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(MKE_pct, EKE_pct), 
               names_to = "Component", values_to = "Percentage") %>%
  mutate(Component = gsub("_pct", "", Component)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = date, y = Percentage, fill = Component)) +
  geom_area(alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("MKE" = "#1E88E5", "EKE" = "#D32F2F")) +
  labs(
    title = "D) Energy Partitioning",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Percentage of Total KE (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "top")

p3 <- (panel_a | panel_b) / (panel_c | panel_d) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Reynolds Decomposition Validation: KE = MKE + EKE",
    subtitle = sprintf("Pan-Arctic Mean (≥60°N) | MKE/EKE Ratio: %.2f ± %.2f", 
                      mean(mke_ts/eke_ts), sd(mke_ts/eke_ts)),
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5)
    )
  )

ggsave(file.path(plot_dir, "Fig3_Reynolds_Validation.png"), 
       plot = p3, width = 14, height = 10, dpi = 300)

cat("  ✓ Saved: Fig3_Reynolds_Validation.png\n")

# ============================================================================
# PLOT 4: CLIMATOLOGICAL MAPS (DJF EXAMPLE)
# ============================================================================

cat("\nGenerating Plot 4: Climatological Maps...\n")

# Calculate climatological mean (e.g., DJF average)
# Select DJF months (Dec=12, Jan=1, Feb=2)
month_indices <- which(month(dates) %in% c(12, 1, 2))

# Calculate DJF means: input is [time, lat, lon], output is [lat, lon]
mke_djf_mean <- apply(mke_permuted[month_indices, , ], c(2, 3), mean, na.rm = TRUE)
eke_djf_mean <- apply(eke_permuted[month_indices, , ], c(2, 3), mean, na.rm = TRUE)

# Result is [lat, lon] with dimensions [35, 360]
# as.vector() in R is column-major, so varies lat first (down columns), then lon
# Therefore use expand.grid(lat, lon) so lat varies first to match
mke_df <- expand.grid(lat = lat, lon = lon) %>%
  mutate(MKE = as.vector(mke_djf_mean))

eke_df <- expand.grid(lat = lat, lon = lon) %>%
  mutate(EKE = as.vector(eke_djf_mean))

# MKE map
map_mke <- ggplot(mke_df, aes(x = lon, y = lat, fill = MKE)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_sf(data = world, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.3, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "plasma", name = "MKE\n(m²/s²)") +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-180, 180), ylim = c(60, 90), crs = "+proj=stere +lat_0=90") +
  labs(title = "A) Mean Kinetic Energy (MKE)", x = "", y = "") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

# EKE map
map_eke <- ggplot(eke_df, aes(x = lon, y = lat, fill = EKE)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_sf(data = world, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.3, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "magma", name = "EKE\n(m²/s²)") +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-180, 180), ylim = c(60, 90), crs = "+proj=stere +lat_0=90") +
  labs(title = "B) Eddy Kinetic Energy (EKE)", x = "", y = "") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

# Ratio map
ratio_df <- mke_df %>%
  mutate(Ratio = MKE / eke_df$EKE)

map_ratio <- ggplot(ratio_df, aes(x = lon, y = lat, fill = Ratio)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_sf(data = world, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.3, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "viridis", name = "MKE/EKE\nRatio", 
                       limits = c(0, 10), oob = scales::squish) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-180, 180), ylim = c(60, 90), crs = "+proj=stere +lat_0=90") +
  labs(title = "C) MKE/EKE Ratio", x = "", y = "") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

p4 <- (map_mke | map_eke) / map_ratio +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Climatological Mean: Winter (DJF) Kinetic Energy Fields",
    subtitle = "1958-2024 Average | Stereographic Projection",
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5)
    )
  )

ggsave(file.path(plot_dir, "Fig4_Climatological_Maps.png"), 
       plot = p4, width = 14, height = 12, dpi = 300)

cat("  ✓ Saved: Fig4_Climatological_Maps.png\n")

# ============================================================================
# PLOT 5: SEASONAL CYCLE VALIDATION
# ============================================================================

cat("\nGenerating Plot 5: Seasonal Cycle...\n")

seasonal_df <- data.frame(
  date = dates,
  month = month(dates),
  MKE = mke_ts,
  EKE = eke_ts
) %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarize(
    MKE_mean = mean(MKE, na.rm = TRUE),
    MKE_sd = sd(MKE, na.rm = TRUE),
    EKE_mean = mean(EKE, na.rm = TRUE),
    EKE_sd = sd(EKE, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(month_label = month.abb[month])

# Panel A: MKE seasonal cycle
panel_a <- ggplot(seasonal_df, aes(x = month, y = MKE_mean)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = MKE_mean - MKE_sd, ymax = MKE_mean + MKE_sd),
              fill = "#1E88E5", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(color = "#1E88E5", linewidth = 1.5) +
  geom_point(color = "#1E88E5", size = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = month.abb) +
  labs(
    title = "A) MKE Seasonal Cycle",
    x = "Month",
    y = "MKE (m²/s²)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

# Panel B: EKE seasonal cycle
panel_b <- ggplot(seasonal_df, aes(x = month, y = EKE_mean)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = EKE_mean - EKE_sd, ymax = EKE_mean + EKE_sd),
              fill = "#D32F2F", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(color = "#D32F2F", linewidth = 1.5) +
  geom_point(color = "#D32F2F", size = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = month.abb) +
  labs(
    title = "B) EKE Seasonal Cycle",
    x = "Month",
    y = "EKE (m²/s²)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

# Panel C: Ratio seasonal cycle
panel_c <- seasonal_df %>%
  mutate(Ratio = MKE_mean / EKE_mean) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = month, y = Ratio)) +
  geom_line(color = "#7B1FA2", linewidth = 1.5) +
  geom_point(color = "#7B1FA2", size = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = month.abb) +
  labs(
    title = "C) MKE/EKE Ratio Seasonal Cycle",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Ratio (dimensionless)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

p5 <- (panel_a / panel_b / panel_c) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Seasonal Cycle Validation: Pan-Arctic Kinetic Energy",
    subtitle = "Mean ± 1 SD across 67 years (1958-2024)",
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5)
    )
  )

ggsave(file.path(plot_dir, "Fig5_Seasonal_Cycle.png"), 
       plot = p5, width = 12, height = 12, dpi = 300)

cat("  ✓ Saved: Fig5_Seasonal_Cycle.png\n")

# ============================================================================
# SUMMARY STATISTICS
# ============================================================================

cat("\nGenerating summary statistics...\n")

summary_stats <- data.frame(
  Metric = c("Temporal Coverage", "Spatial Resolution", "Data Points", 
             "Mean MKE", "Mean EKE", "Mean Ratio", "Data Completeness"),
  Value = c(
    sprintf("%d years (%d-%d)", 
            length(unique(year(dates))), min(year(dates)), max(year(dates))),
    "0.25° × 0.25°",
    sprintf("%d months × %d gridpoints = %d total", 
            length(dates), length(lat) * length(lon), 
            length(dates) * length(lat) * length(lon)),
    sprintf("%.2f ± %.2f m²/s²", mean(mke_ts), sd(mke_ts)),
    sprintf("%.2f ± %.2f m²/s²", mean(eke_ts), sd(eke_ts)),
    sprintf("%.2f ± %.2f", mean(mke_ts/eke_ts), sd(mke_ts/eke_ts)),
    sprintf("%.2f%%", mean(completeness$pct_complete))
  )
)

write.csv(summary_stats, file.path(plot_dir, "Phase1_Summary_Statistics.csv"), 
          row.names = FALSE)

# ============================================================================
# FINAL SUMMARY
# ============================================================================

cat("\n", rep("=", 80), "\n")
cat("PHASE 1 DIAGNOSTICS COMPLETE!\n")
cat(rep("=", 80), "\n\n")

cat("Generated Figures:\n")
cat("  1. Fig1_Spatial_Domain.png - Arctic domain and regional masks\n")
cat("  2. Fig2_Temporal_Coverage.png - Data completeness assessment\n")
cat("  3. Fig3_Reynolds_Validation.png - Reynolds decomposition checks\n")
cat("  4. Fig4_Climatological_Maps.png - DJF mean fields\n")
cat("  5. Fig5_Seasonal_Cycle.png - Monthly climatology\n\n")

cat(glue::glue("All files saved to: {plot_dir}\n\n"))

cat("Summary Statistics:\n")
print(knitr::kable(summary_stats, format = "markdown"))

cat("\n", rep("=", 80), "\n")
cat("DATA QUALITY ASSESSMENT\n")
cat(rep("=", 80), "\n\n")

cat("✓ Temporal Coverage: COMPLETE\n")
cat(glue::glue("  → {length(dates)} months from {min(year(dates))} to {max(year(dates))}\n"))
cat(glue::glue("  → Mean completeness: {round(mean(completeness$pct_complete), 2)}%\n\n"))
```

```{r EKE-MKE-polar-plots}
# ============================================================================
# PHASE 1: CLIMATOLOGICAL MAPS - THREE SEPARATE FIGURES
#
# PURPOSE: Create 3 separate figures with larger, more visible maps:
#   Figure 1: Annual Mean (1 row × 3 panels)
#   Figure 2: Winter Seasons - DJF, DJFM, FMA (3 rows × 3 panels)
#   Figure 3: Other Seasons - MAM, JJA, SON (3 rows × 3 panels)
#
# ============================================================================

# --- SETUP ---
processed_dir <- "E:/ERA5_data/processed"
plot_dir <- file.path(processed_dir, "phase1_diagnostics")
if (!dir.exists(plot_dir)) dir.create(plot_dir, recursive = TRUE)

cat("\n", rep("=", 80), "\n")
cat("PHASE 1: THREE-FIGURE CLIMATOLOGY SET\n")
cat(rep("=", 80), "\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# DEFINE SEASONS
# ============================================================================

season_definitions <- list(
  Annual = list(months = 1:12, name = "Annual Mean", abbr = "ANN", label = "Annual Mean"),
  DJF = list(months = c(12, 1, 2), name = "Winter", abbr = "DJF", label = "Winter (DJF)"),
  DJFM = list(months = c(12, 1, 2, 3), name = "Extended Winter", abbr = "DJFM", label = "Extended Winter (DJFM)"),
  FMA = list(months = c(2, 3, 4), name = "Late Winter-Spring", abbr = "FMA", label = "Late Winter-Spring (FMA)"),
  MAM = list(months = c(3, 4, 5), name = "Spring", abbr = "MAM", label = "Spring (MAM)"),
  JJA = list(months = c(6, 7, 8), name = "Summer", abbr = "JJA", label = "Summer (JJA)"),
  SON = list(months = c(9, 10, 11), name = "Autumn", abbr = "SON", label = "Autumn (SON)")
)

# Figure groupings
fig1_seasons <- c("Annual")
fig2_seasons <- c("DJF", "DJFM", "FMA")  # Winter-focused
fig3_seasons <- c("MAM", "JJA", "SON")   # Other seasons

# ============================================================================
# LOAD DATA
# ============================================================================

cat("Loading NetCDF data...\n")

nc_mke <- nc_open(file.path(processed_dir, "ERA5_MKE_monthly_1958-2024.nc"))
nc_eke <- nc_open(file.path(processed_dir, "ERA5_EKE_monthly_1958-2024.nc"))

mke <- ncvar_get(nc_mke, "mke")
eke <- ncvar_get(nc_eke, "eke")
lat <- ncvar_get(nc_mke, "latitude")
lon <- ncvar_get(nc_mke, "longitude")

nc_close(nc_mke)
nc_close(nc_eke)

n_times <- dim(mke)[3]
dates <- seq(as.Date("1958-01-01"), by = "month", length.out = n_times)

cat("  Permuting dimensions...\n")
mke_permuted <- aperm(mke, c(3, 2, 1))
eke_permuted <- aperm(eke, c(3, 2, 1))

rm(mke, eke)
gc(verbose = FALSE)

# ============================================================================
# CALCULATE ALL SEASONAL MEANS AND GLOBAL RANGES
# ============================================================================

cat("\nCalculating seasonal means and global ranges...\n")

seasonal_data <- list()
all_mke <- c()
all_eke <- c()
all_ratio <- c()

for (season_name in names(season_definitions)) {
  months <- season_definitions[[season_name]]$months
  season_indices <- which(month(dates) %in% months)
  
  mke_season <- apply(mke_permuted[season_indices, , ], c(2, 3), mean, na.rm = TRUE)
  eke_season <- apply(eke_permuted[season_indices, , ], c(2, 3), mean, na.rm = TRUE)
  ratio_season <- mke_season / eke_season
  
  seasonal_data[[season_name]] <- list(
    mke = mke_season,
    eke = eke_season,
    ratio = ratio_season
  )
  
  all_mke <- c(all_mke, as.vector(mke_season))
  all_eke <- c(all_eke, as.vector(eke_season))
  all_ratio <- c(all_ratio, as.vector(ratio_season))
  
  cat(sprintf("  %s: MKE=%.1f, EKE=%.1f, Ratio=%.2f\n",
              season_definitions[[season_name]]$label,
              mean(mke_season, na.rm = TRUE),
              mean(eke_season, na.rm = TRUE),
              mean(ratio_season, na.rm = TRUE)))
}

# CRITICAL: Calculate GLOBAL ranges for uniform color scales across all figures
mke_global_range <- range(all_mke, na.rm = TRUE)
eke_global_range <- range(all_eke, na.rm = TRUE)
ratio_global_range <- c(0, 10)

cat(sprintf("\n*** GLOBAL COLOR RANGES (used for all 3 figures) ***\n"))
cat(sprintf("  MKE: %.1f to %.1f m²/s²\n", mke_global_range[1], mke_global_range[2]))
cat(sprintf("  EKE: %.1f to %.1f m²/s²\n", eke_global_range[1], eke_global_range[2]))
cat(sprintf("  Ratio: %.1f to %.1f\n\n", ratio_global_range[1], ratio_global_range[2]))

# ============================================================================
# PREPARE CARTOGRAPHIC ELEMENTS
# ============================================================================

cat("Preparing cartographic elements...\n")

arctic_crs <- "+proj=laea +lat_0=90 +lon_0=0"
view_radius <- 3700000
plot_radius <- 4400000

circle_mask <- st_sfc(st_point(c(0, 0)), crs = arctic_crs) %>%
  st_buffer(dist = view_radius)

square_box <- st_as_sfc(st_bbox(c(
  xmin = -plot_radius, xmax = plot_radius,
  ymin = -plot_radius, ymax = plot_radius
), crs = arctic_crs))
inverse_mask <- st_difference(square_box, circle_mask)

world <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")
world_polar <- st_transform(world, crs = arctic_crs)

graticules <- st_graticule(
  lon = seq(-180, 180, by = 60),
  lat = c(60, 70, 80),
  crs = 4326
) %>%
  st_transform(crs = arctic_crs)

lat_labels <- data.frame(lon = 180, lat = c(60, 70, 80)) %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) %>%
  st_transform(crs = arctic_crs)
lat_labels$label <- c("60°N", "70°N", "80°N")

lon_labels <- data.frame(lon = seq(0, 300, by = 60), lat = 55) %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) %>%
  st_transform(crs = arctic_crs)
lon_labels$label <- c("0°", "60°E", "120°E", "180°W", "120°W", "60°W")

cat("  ✓ Cartographic elements prepared\n")

# ============================================================================
# FUNCTION: CREATE SINGLE MAP WITH GLOBAL COLOR SCALES
# ============================================================================

create_map <- function(data_masked, variable, variable_name, show_legend = TRUE) {
  
  # Use GLOBAL ranges for all maps
  if (variable == "mke") {
    color_range <- mke_global_range
    color_option <- "plasma"
  } else if (variable == "eke") {
    color_range <- eke_global_range
    color_option <- "magma"
  } else {  # ratio
    color_range <- ratio_global_range
    color_option <- "viridis"
  }
  
  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_stars(data = data_masked, aes(fill = .data[[variable]]), na.rm = TRUE) +
    scale_fill_viridis(
      name = variable_name,
      option = color_option,
      na.value = "transparent",
      limits = color_range,
      breaks = if (variable == "ratio") seq(0, 10, by = 2) else pretty(color_range, n = 5),
      oob = if (variable == "ratio") scales::squish else scales::censor,
      guide = if (show_legend) guide_colorbar(barwidth = 1, barheight = 10) else "none"
    ) +
    geom_sf(data = world_polar, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_sf(data = graticules, color = "gray50", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.25) +
    geom_sf(data = inverse_mask, fill = "white", color = NA) +
    geom_sf_text(data = lat_labels, aes(label = label), size = 3, color = "black", hjust = 1.2) +
    geom_sf_text(data = lon_labels, aes(label = label), size = 3, color = "black") +
    coord_sf(xlim = c(-plot_radius, plot_radius), 
             ylim = c(-plot_radius, plot_radius), expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = variable_name) +
    theme_void(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = 14),
      legend.position = if (show_legend) "right" else "none",
      legend.key.width = unit(0.8, "cm"),
      legend.key.height = unit(2, "cm"),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "gray95", color = NA),
      plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5)
    )
  
  return(p)
}

# ============================================================================
# FUNCTION: CREATE SEASON PANEL (3 maps: MKE, EKE, Ratio)
# ============================================================================

create_season_panel <- function(season_name, show_titles = FALSE) {
  
  season_data <- seasonal_data[[season_name]]
  
  # Create stars object
  lon_vec <- as.vector(lon)
  lat_vec <- as.vector(lat)
  
  data_list <- list(
    mke = t(season_data$mke),
    eke = t(season_data$eke),
    ratio = t(season_data$ratio)
  )
  
  dims <- st_dimensions(x = lon_vec, y = lat_vec)
  clim_stars <- st_as_stars(data_list, dimensions = dims) %>%
    st_set_crs(4326)
  
  # Warp and mask
  clim_polar <- st_warp(clim_stars, crs = arctic_crs)
  clim_polar_masked <- clim_polar[circle_mask]
  
  # Create 3 maps
  p_mke <- create_map(clim_polar_masked, "mke", if (show_titles) "MKE (m²/s²)" else NULL, show_legend = TRUE)
  p_eke <- create_map(clim_polar_masked, "eke", if (show_titles) "EKE (m²/s²)" else NULL, show_legend = TRUE)
  p_ratio <- create_map(clim_polar_masked, "ratio", if (show_titles) "MKE/EKE Ratio" else NULL, show_legend = TRUE)
  
  return(list(mke = p_mke, eke = p_eke, ratio = p_ratio))
}

# ============================================================================
# FIGURE 1: ANNUAL MEAN
# ============================================================================

cat("\n=== FIGURE 1: ANNUAL MEAN ===\n")

annual_maps <- create_season_panel("Annual", show_titles = TRUE)

fig1 <- annual_maps$mke + annual_maps$eke + annual_maps$ratio +
  plot_layout(ncol = 3) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Arctic Kinetic Energy Climatology: Annual Mean (1958-2024)",
    subtitle = "Lambert Azimuthal Equal-Area Projection | Arctic Domain (≥60°N)",
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 13, hjust = 0.5)
    )
  )

output_file1 <- file.path(plot_dir, "Fig1_Climatology_ANNUAL.png")

# ============================================================================

cat("\n=== FIGURE 2: WINTER SEASONS ===\n")

djf_maps <- create_season_panel("DJF", show_titles = TRUE)
djfm_maps <- create_season_panel("DJFM", show_titles = FALSE)
fma_maps <- create_season_panel("FMA", show_titles = FALSE)

# Create season label plots
label_djf <- ggplot() +
  annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 0.5, label = "Winter\n(DJF)", 
           size = 6, fontface = "bold", hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5) +

label_fma <- ggplot() +

# Row 1: DJF (with label + 3 maps)
row1 <- label_djf + djf_maps$mke + djf_maps$eke + djf_maps$ratio +

# Row 2: DJFM (with label + 3 maps)
row2 <- label_djfm + djfm_maps$mke + djfm_maps$eke + djfm_maps$ratio +
  plot_layout(ncol = 4, widths = c(0.3, 1, 1, 1))

# Row 3: FMA (with label + 3 maps)
row3 <- label_fma + fma_maps$mke + fma_maps$eke + fma_maps$ratio +
  plot_layout(ncol = 4, widths = c(0.3, 1, 1, 1))

fig2 <- row1 / row2 / row3 +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Arctic Kinetic Energy Climatology: Winter Seasons (1958-2024)",
    subtitle = "Lambert Azimuthal Equal-Area Projection | Uniform color scales with Annual and Other Seasons",
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 13, hjust = 0.5)
    )
  )

output_file2 <- file.path(plot_dir, "Fig2_Climatology_WINTER_SEASONS.png")
ggsave(output_file2, fig2, width = 22, height = 20, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
cat(sprintf("  ✓ Saved: %s\n", basename(output_file2)))

# ============================================================================
# FIGURE 3: OTHER SEASONS (MAM, JJA, SON)
# ============================================================================

cat("\n=== FIGURE 3: OTHER SEASONS ===\n")

mam_maps <- create_season_panel("MAM", show_titles = TRUE)
jja_maps <- create_season_panel("JJA", show_titles = FALSE)
son_maps <- create_season_panel("SON", show_titles = FALSE)

# Create season label plots
label_mam <- ggplot() +
  annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 0.5, label = "Spring\n(MAM)", 
           size = 6, fontface = "bold", hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))

label_jja <- ggplot() +
  annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 0.5, label = "Summer\n(JJA)", 
           size = 6, fontface = "bold", hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))

label_son <- ggplot() +
  annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 0.5, label = "Autumn\n(SON)", 
           size = 6, fontface = "bold", hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))

# Row 1: MAM (with label + 3 maps)
row1 <- label_mam + mam_maps$mke + mam_maps$eke + mam_maps$ratio +
  plot_layout(ncol = 4, widths = c(0.3, 1, 1, 1))

# Row 2: JJA (with label + 3 maps)
row2 <- label_jja + jja_maps$mke + jja_maps$eke + jja_maps$ratio +

fig3 <- row1 / row2 / row3 +

    subtitle = "Lambert Azimuthal Equal-Area Projection | Uniform color scales with Annual and Winter Seasons",
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),

output_file3 <- file.path(plot_dir, "Fig3_Climatology_OTHER_SEASONS.png")
ggsave(output_file3, fig3, width = 22, height = 20, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

# ============================================================================
# SUMMARY
# ============================================================================

cat("\n", rep("=", 80), "\n")
cat("THREE-FIGURE CLIMATOLOGY SET COMPLETE!\n")
cat(rep("=", 80), "\n\n")

cat("Generated Figures:\n")

cat(sprintf("  2. %s\n", basename(output_file2)))

cat("Figure specifications:\n")
```

```{r trend}
# ============================================================================
# PHASE 1: PRIMARY TIME SERIES VISUALIZATION
# Pan-Arctic Storminess Index (1958-2024)
# ============================================================================
#
# PURPOSE: Create the foundational time series plot showing:
#   - Monthly area-weighted storminess index
#   - 12-month running mean to reveal interannual variability
#   - Long-term mean reference line
#
# INPUT: Requires 'storm_df' data frame from Phase 1 Section 1.3
#        with columns: date, storminess
# ============================================================================

# --- SETUP ---
plot_dir <- here("Data", "processed", "phase1_diagnostics")
if (!dir.exists(plot_dir)) dir.create(plot_dir, recursive = TRUE)

cat("\n", rep("=", 80), "\n")
cat("PHASE 1: PRIMARY TIME SERIES VISUALIZATION\n")
cat(rep("=", 80), "\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 1: CALCULATE DERIVED TIME SERIES COMPONENTS
# ============================================================================

cat("Calculating derived time series components...\n")

# 1.1 Calculate 12-month centered rolling mean (interannual signal)
storm_df <- storm_df %>%
  mutate(
    rolling_mean_12m = rollmean(storminess, k = 12, fill = NA, align = "center")
  )

# 1.2 Calculate long-term mean (climatological baseline)
long_term_mean <- mean(storm_df$storminess, na.rm = TRUE)

# 1.3 Calculate overall statistics for annotation
min_value <- min(storm_df$storminess, na.rm = TRUE)
max_value <- max(storm_df$storminess, na.rm = TRUE)
std_dev <- sd(storm_df$storminess, na.rm = TRUE)

cat(sprintf("  Long-term mean: %.2f m⁴/s⁴\n", long_term_mean))
cat(sprintf("  Standard deviation: %.2f m⁴/s⁴\n", std_dev))
cat(sprintf("  Range: %.2f to %.2f m⁴/s⁴\n\n", min_value, max_value))

# ============================================================================
# STEP 2: CREATE THE PRIMARY TIME SERIES PLOT
# ============================================================================

cat("Creating primary time series visualization...\n")

p <- ggplot(storm_df, aes(x = date)) +
  
  # --- LONG-TERM MEAN LINE ---
  geom_hline(yintercept = long_term_mean, 
             linetype = "dashed", color = "black", linewidth = 0.8, 
             alpha = 0.8) +
  
  # --- MONTHLY TIME SERIES (raw data) ---
  geom_line(aes(y = storminess), 
            color = "gray30", linewidth = 0.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  
  # --- 12-MONTH ROLLING MEAN (smooth interannual signal) ---
  geom_line(aes(y = rolling_mean_12m), 
            color = "#D62728", linewidth = 1.3) +
  
  # --- SCALES AND LABELS ---
  scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "5 years",
    date_labels = "%Y",
    expand = c(0.01, 0)
  ) +
  
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, ceiling(max_value/50)*50, by = 50),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.05))
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Pan-Arctic Storminess Index: 1958–2024",
    subtitle = "Monthly variance of synoptic-scale EKE | Area-weighted average (≥60°N)",
    x = "Year",
    y = expression(paste("Storminess Index (m"^4, " s"^{-4}, ")"))
  ) +
  
  # --- THEME ---
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, 
                              margin = margin(b = 8)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, hjust = 0.5, 
                                 margin = margin(b = 15), color = "gray30"),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold", margin = margin(t = 10)),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold", margin = margin(r = 10)),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 11),
    panel.grid.minor = element_line(linewidth = 0.2, color = "gray90"),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(linewidth = 0.4, color = "gray85"),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#FFF9F0", color = NA),  # Soft beige
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.margin = margin(15, 15, 15, 15)
  )

# ============================================================================
# STEP 3: ADD LEGEND FOR LINE TYPES
# ============================================================================

# Create a manual legend in the upper right corner
# Use numeric date arithmetic instead of lubridate periods
legend_x_start <- as.Date("2014-01-01")
legend_x_end <- as.Date("2016-01-01")  # 2 years later
legend_x_text <- as.Date("2016-07-01")  # 2.5 years later
legend_y_top <- max_value * 0.98
legend_y_spacing <- max_value * 0.05

p <- p +
  # Monthly values legend
  annotate("segment", 
           x = legend_x_start, xend = legend_x_end,
           y = legend_y_top, yend = legend_y_top,
           color = "gray30", linewidth = 0.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  annotate("text", 
           x = legend_x_text, y = legend_y_top,
           label = "Monthly values", 
           hjust = 0, size = 3.5, color = "gray20") +
  
  # 12-month running mean legend
  annotate("segment", 
           x = legend_x_start, xend = legend_x_end,
           y = legend_y_top - legend_y_spacing, 
           yend = legend_y_top - legend_y_spacing,
           color = "#D62728", linewidth = 1.3) +
  annotate("text", 
           x = legend_x_text, 
           y = legend_y_top - legend_y_spacing,
           label = "12-month running mean", 
           hjust = 0, size = 3.5, color = "gray20") +

  # Long-term mean line legend (THIRD item - needs 2x spacing!)
  annotate("segment", 
           x = legend_x_start, xend = legend_x_end, 
           y = legend_y_top - 2 * legend_y_spacing,  
           yend = legend_y_top - 2 * legend_y_spacing,  
           linetype = "dashed", color = "black", linewidth = 0.8, alpha = 0.8) +
  annotate("text", 
           x = legend_x_text, 
           y = legend_y_top - 2 * legend_y_spacing, 
           label = sprintf("Long-term mean: %.1f m⁴ s⁻⁴", long_term_mean),
           hjust = 0, size = 3.5, color = "gray20")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 4: SAVE THE PLOT
# ============================================================================

output_file <- file.path(plot_dir, "Fig_Primary_TimeSeries_Storminess.png")

ggsave(
  filename = output_file,
  plot = p,
  width = 16,
  height = 8,
  dpi = 300,
  bg = "white"
)

cat(sprintf("  ✓ Primary time series plot saved: %s\n\n", basename(output_file)))

# ============================================================================
# STEP 5: SUMMARY STATISTICS
# ============================================================================

cat(rep("=", 80), "\n")
cat("TIME SERIES VISUALIZATION COMPLETE\n")
cat(rep("=", 80), "\n\n")

cat("Summary Statistics (1958-2024):\n")
cat(rep("-", 50), "\n")
cat(sprintf("  Mean:               %.2f m⁴/s⁴\n", long_term_mean))
cat(sprintf("  Standard Deviation: %.2f m⁴/s⁴\n", std_dev))
cat(sprintf("  Minimum:            %.2f m⁴/s⁴\n", min_value))
cat(sprintf("  Maximum:            %.2f m⁴/s⁴\n", max_value))
cat(sprintf("  Range:              %.2f m⁴/s⁴\n", max_value - min_value))
cat(sprintf("  CV (σ/μ):           %.3f (%.1f%%)\n\n", 
            std_dev / long_term_mean,
            100 * std_dev / long_term_mean))

cat("Generated File:\n")
cat(sprintf("  %s\n\n", basename(output_file)))

cat("Plot Features:\n")
cat("  ✓ Monthly time series (gray line)\n")
cat("  ✓ 12-month running mean (red line) - reveals interannual variability\n")
cat("  ✓ Long-term mean reference line (dashed) - shows deviations\n")
cat("  ✓ Clean beige background for visual comfort\n")
cat("  ✓ In-plot legend in upper right corner\n")
cat("  ✓ Professional formatting for publication\n\n")

cat("Interpretation Guide:\n")
```

```{r stl-decomposition}
# ============================================================================
# PHASE 1: SEASONAL DECOMPOSITION ANALYSIS
# Pan-Arctic Storminess Index (1958-2024)
# ============================================================================
#
# PURPOSE: Decompose the time series into:
#   - Trend component (long-term, slow variations)
#   - Seasonal component (annual cycle)
#   - Remainder/Irregular component (short-term fluctuations)
#
# METHOD: STL (Seasonal and Trend decomposition using Loess)
#   - More robust than classical decomposition
#   - Handles non-linear trends
#   - Allows seasonal component to vary over time
#
# INPUT: Requires 'storm_ts_obj' from Phase 1 Section 1.3
# ============================================================================

# --- SETUP ---
plot_dir <- here("Data", "processed", "phase1_diagnostics")
if (!dir.exists(plot_dir)) dir.create(plot_dir, recursive = TRUE)

cat("\n", rep("=", 80), "\n")
cat("PHASE 1: SEASONAL DECOMPOSITION ANALYSIS\n")
cat(rep("=", 80), "\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 1: PERFORM STL DECOMPOSITION
# ============================================================================

cat("Performing STL decomposition...\n")

# STL decomposition with robust fitting
# s.window = "periodic" assumes seasonal pattern doesn't change over time
# s.window = 13 or higher allows it to vary (13 = uses 13 years of data)
# t.window = length of smoothing window for trend (controls smoothness)

stl_result <- stl(storm_ts_obj, 
                  s.window = "periodic",  # Seasonal pattern assumed constant
                  t.window = 15,          # Trend smoothing (15 years)
                  robust = TRUE)          # Robust to outliers

# Extract components
decomp_df <- data.frame(
  date = storm_df$date,
  observed = as.numeric(storm_ts_obj),
  trend = as.numeric(stl_result$time.series[, "trend"]),
  seasonal = as.numeric(stl_result$time.series[, "seasonal"]),
  remainder = as.numeric(stl_result$time.series[, "remainder"])
)

# Calculate variance explained by each component
var_total <- var(decomp_df$observed, na.rm = TRUE)
var_trend <- var(decomp_df$trend, na.rm = TRUE)
var_seasonal <- var(decomp_df$seasonal, na.rm = TRUE)
var_remainder <- var(decomp_df$remainder, na.rm = TRUE)

pct_trend <- 100 * var_trend / var_total
pct_seasonal <- 100 * var_seasonal / var_total
pct_remainder <- 100 * var_remainder / var_total

cat(sprintf("  Variance decomposition:\n"))
cat(sprintf("    Trend:     %.2f%% of total variance\n", pct_trend))
cat(sprintf("    Seasonal:  %.2f%% of total variance\n", pct_seasonal))
cat(sprintf("    Remainder: %.2f%% of total variance\n\n", pct_remainder))

# ============================================================================
# STEP 2: CREATE SEASONAL CLIMATOLOGY (MEAN ANNUAL CYCLE)
# ============================================================================

cat("Calculating mean seasonal cycle...\n")

# Extract just the unique seasonal pattern (12 months)
seasonal_cycle <- decomp_df %>%
  mutate(month = format(date, "%b")) %>%
  mutate(month = factor(month, levels = c("Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun",
                                           "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec"))) %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarise(
    seasonal_mean = mean(seasonal, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Calculate range of seasonal component
seasonal_range <- max(seasonal_cycle$seasonal_mean) - min(seasonal_cycle$seasonal_mean)
peak_month <- seasonal_cycle$month[which.max(seasonal_cycle$seasonal_mean)]
trough_month <- seasonal_cycle$month[which.min(seasonal_cycle$seasonal_mean)]

cat(sprintf("  Peak storminess month: %s (%.2f m⁴/s⁴ above annual mean)\n", 
            peak_month, max(seasonal_cycle$seasonal_mean)))
cat(sprintf("  Lowest storminess month: %s (%.2f m⁴/s⁴ below annual mean)\n", 
            trough_month, min(seasonal_cycle$seasonal_mean)))
cat(sprintf("  Seasonal amplitude: %.2f m⁴/s⁴\n\n", seasonal_range))

# ============================================================================
# STEP 3: CREATE FOUR-PANEL DECOMPOSITION PLOT
# ============================================================================

cat("Creating decomposition visualization...\n")

# Define common x-axis settings
x_scale <- scale_x_date(
  date_breaks = "5 years",
  date_labels = "%Y",
  expand = c(0.01, 0)
)

# Common theme
common_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", hjust = 0),
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 9),
    panel.grid.minor = element_line(linewidth = 0.2, color = "gray90"),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(linewidth = 0.3, color = "gray85"),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#FFF9F0", color = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.margin = margin(5, 10, 5, 10)
  )

# --- PANEL 1: OBSERVED DATA ---
p1 <- ggplot(decomp_df, aes(x = date, y = observed)) +
  geom_line(color = "gray30", linewidth = 0.4) +
  x_scale +
  labs(
    title = "A. Observed Time Series",
    y = expression(paste("Storminess (m"^4, " s"^{-4}, ")"))
  ) +
  common_theme

# --- PANEL 2: TREND COMPONENT ---
p2 <- ggplot(decomp_df, aes(x = date, y = trend)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(decomp_df$trend, na.rm = TRUE), 
             linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_line(color = "#1F77B4", linewidth = 0.8) +
  x_scale +
  labs(
    title = sprintf("B. Trend Component (%.1f%% of variance)", pct_trend),
    y = expression(paste("Trend (m"^4, " s"^{-4}, ")"))
  ) +
  common_theme

# --- PANEL 3: SEASONAL COMPONENT ---
p3 <- ggplot(decomp_df, aes(x = date, y = seasonal)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "solid", color = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_line(color = "#2CA02C", linewidth = 0.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  x_scale +
  labs(
    title = sprintf("C. Seasonal Component (%.1f%% of variance)", pct_seasonal),
    y = expression(paste("Seasonal (m"^4, " s"^{-4}, ")"))
  ) +
  common_theme

# --- PANEL 4: REMAINDER (IRREGULAR) COMPONENT ---
p4 <- ggplot(decomp_df, aes(x = date, y = remainder)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "solid", color = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_line(color = "#D62728", linewidth = 0.3, alpha = 0.6) +
  x_scale +
  scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "5 years",
    date_labels = "%Y",
    expand = c(0.01, 0)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = sprintf("D. Remainder Component (%.1f%% of variance)", pct_remainder),
    y = expression(paste("Remainder (m"^4, " s"^{-4}, ")")),
    x = "Year"
  ) +
  common_theme +
  theme(axis.title.x = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold", margin = margin(t = 5)))

# --- COMBINE PANELS ---
combined_plot <- grid.arrange(
  p1, p2, p3, p4,
  ncol = 1,
  top = grid::textGrob(
    "STL Decomposition: Pan-Arctic Storminess Index (1958–2024)",
    gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 16, fontface = "bold")
  ),
  bottom = grid::textGrob(
    "STL method: s.window = 'periodic', t.window = 15 years, robust = TRUE",
    gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 9, col = "gray40"),
    x = 0.5, hjust = 0.5
  )
)

# ============================================================================
# STEP 4: SAVE DECOMPOSITION PLOT
# ============================================================================

output_file <- file.path(plot_dir, "Fig_Seasonal_Decomposition_STL.png")

ggsave(
  filename = output_file,
  plot = combined_plot,
  width = 14,
  height = 11,
  dpi = 300,
  bg = "white"
)

cat(sprintf("  ✓ STL decomposition plot saved: %s\n\n", basename(output_file)))

# ============================================================================
# STEP 5: CREATE MEAN SEASONAL CYCLE PLOT (CLIMATOLOGY)
# ============================================================================

cat("Creating mean seasonal cycle plot...\n")

p_seasonal <- ggplot(seasonal_cycle, aes(x = month, y = seasonal_mean)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_line(aes(group = 1), color = "#2CA02C", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(color = "#2CA02C", size = 3, shape = 16) +
  geom_point(data = subset(seasonal_cycle, month == peak_month),
             color = "#D62728", size = 4, shape = 17) +
  geom_point(data = subset(seasonal_cycle, month == trough_month),
             color = "#1F77B4", size = 4, shape = 17) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = pretty(seasonal_cycle$seasonal_mean, n = 8)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Mean Seasonal Cycle of Arctic Storminess (1958–2024)",
    subtitle = sprintf("Peak: %s | Trough: %s | Amplitude: %.2f m⁴ s⁻⁴", 
                      peak_month, trough_month, seasonal_range),
    x = "Month",
    y = expression(paste("Seasonal Anomaly (m"^4, " s"^{-4}, ")"))
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 5)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 15), 
                                 color = "gray30"),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", margin = margin(t = 10)),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", margin = margin(r = 10)),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(linewidth = 0.4, color = "gray85"),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#FFF9F0", color = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.margin = margin(15, 15, 15, 15)
  ) +
  annotate("text", x = which(seasonal_cycle$month == peak_month), 
           y = max(seasonal_cycle$seasonal_mean) + seasonal_range * 0.1,
           label = "Peak", color = "#D62728", fontface = "bold", size = 3.5) +
  annotate("text", x = which(seasonal_cycle$month == trough_month), 
           y = min(seasonal_cycle$seasonal_mean) - seasonal_range * 0.1,
           label = "Trough", color = "#1F77B4", fontface = "bold", size = 3.5)

output_file_seasonal <- file.path(plot_dir, "Fig_Mean_Seasonal_Cycle.png")

ggsave(
  filename = output_file_seasonal,
  plot = p_seasonal,
  width = 12,
  height = 7,
  dpi = 300,
  bg = "white"
)

cat(sprintf("  ✓ Mean seasonal cycle plot saved: %s\n\n", basename(output_file_seasonal)))

# ============================================================================
# STEP 6: SUMMARY STATISTICS AND DIAGNOSTICS
# ============================================================================

cat(rep("=", 80), "\n")
cat("SEASONAL DECOMPOSITION ANALYSIS COMPLETE\n")
cat(rep("=", 80), "\n\n")

cat("Decomposition Statistics:\n")
cat(rep("-", 50), "\n")
cat(sprintf("STL Method: s.window = 'periodic', t.window = 15 years, robust = TRUE\n\n"))

cat("Variance Partitioning:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Total variance:       %.2f (m⁴/s⁴)²\n", var_total))
cat(sprintf("  Trend variance:       %.2f (m⁴/s⁴)² (%.1f%%)\n", var_trend, pct_trend))
cat(sprintf("  Seasonal variance:    %.2f (m⁴/s⁴)² (%.1f%%)\n", var_seasonal, pct_seasonal))
cat(sprintf("  Remainder variance:   %.2f (m⁴/s⁴)² (%.1f%%)\n\n", var_remainder, pct_remainder))

cat("Seasonal Component Characteristics:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Peak month:           %s\n", peak_month))
cat(sprintf("  Peak magnitude:       %+.2f m⁴/s⁴ (above mean)\n", 
            max(seasonal_cycle$seasonal_mean)))
cat(sprintf("  Trough month:         %s\n", trough_month))
cat(sprintf("  Trough magnitude:     %+.2f m⁴/s⁴ (below mean)\n", 
            min(seasonal_cycle$seasonal_mean)))
cat(sprintf("  Peak-to-trough range: %.2f m⁴/s⁴\n\n", seasonal_range))

cat("Trend Component Characteristics:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Mean:                 %.2f m⁴/s⁴\n", mean(decomp_df$trend, na.rm = TRUE)))
cat(sprintf("  Start value (1958):   %.2f m⁴/s⁴\n", decomp_df$trend[1]))
cat(sprintf("  End value (2024):     %.2f m⁴/s⁴\n", 
            decomp_df$trend[nrow(decomp_df)]))
cat(sprintf("  Total change:         %+.2f m⁴/s⁴\n\n", 
            decomp_df$trend[nrow(decomp_df)] - decomp_df$trend[1]))

cat("Remainder Component Characteristics:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Mean:                 %.2f m⁴/s⁴\n", mean(decomp_df$remainder, na.rm = TRUE)))
cat(sprintf("  Std. deviation:       %.2f m⁴/s⁴\n", sd(decomp_df$remainder, na.rm = TRUE)))
cat(sprintf("  Range:                [%.2f, %.2f] m⁴/s⁴\n\n", 
            min(decomp_df$remainder, na.rm = TRUE),
            max(decomp_df$remainder, na.rm = TRUE)))

cat("Generated Files:\n")
cat(sprintf("  1. %s\n", basename(output_file)))
cat(sprintf("  2. %s\n\n", basename(output_file_seasonal)))

cat("Interpretation Notes:\n")
cat("  • Trend: Shows long-term, smooth variations (interannual to decadal)\n")
cat("  • Seasonal: Shows the repeating annual cycle\n")
cat("  • Remainder: Shows irregular, short-term fluctuations and outliers\n")
cat("  • High seasonal variance indicates strong annual cycle\n")
cat("  • High remainder variance indicates 'noisy' data or extreme events\n\n")

cat(rep("=", 80), "\n")
```
