```{r ACF/PACF}
# ============================================================================
# PHASE 1: ACF AND PACF ANALYSIS
# Pan-Arctic Storminess Index (1958-2024)
# ============================================================================
#
# PURPOSE: Assess the temporal autocorrelation structure:
#   - ACF: Shows correlation with past values at different lags
#   - PACF: Shows direct correlation after removing intermediate effects
#
# INTERPRETATION:
#   - ACF reveals the "memory" in the time series
#   - PACF helps identify AR(p) model order
#   - Both inform the need for autocorrelation-corrected trend tests
#
# INPUT: Requires 'storm_df' data frame with column: storminess
# ============================================================================

# ============================================================================
# PHASE 1: ACF AND PACF ANALYSIS
# Pan-Arctic Storminess Index (1958-2024)
# ============================================================================
#
# PURPOSE: Assess the temporal autocorrelation structure using base R graphics
#
# INPUT: Requires 'storm_df' data frame with column: storminess
# ============================================================================

# --- SETUP ---
plot_dir <- here("Plots", "phase1_diagnostics")  # UPDATED PATH
if (!dir.exists(plot_dir)) dir.create(plot_dir, recursive = TRUE)

cat("\n", rep("=", 80), "\n")
cat("PHASE 1: ACF AND PACF ANALYSIS\n")
cat(rep("=", 80), "\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 1: COMPUTE ACF AND PACF
# ============================================================================

cat("Computing ACF and PACF...\n")

# Set maximum lag (in months)
max_lag <- 36  # 3 years

# Compute ACF
acf_result <- acf(storm_df$storminess, 
                  lag.max = max_lag, 
                  plot = FALSE)

# Compute PACF
pacf_result <- pacf(storm_df$storminess, 
                    lag.max = max_lag, 
                    plot = FALSE)

# Calculate confidence intervals (95%)
n <- length(storm_df$storminess)
ci_level <- 1.96 / sqrt(n)

cat(sprintf("  Number of observations: %d\n", n))
cat(sprintf("  95%% confidence interval: ±%.4f\n\n", ci_level))

# ============================================================================
# STEP 2: EXTRACT KEY STATISTICS
# ============================================================================

cat("Key Autocorrelation Statistics:\n")
cat(rep("-", 50), "\n")

# Lag-1 autocorrelation (most important)
rho_1 <- acf_result$acf[2]  # Index 2 because index 1 is lag 0
cat(sprintf("  ρ₁ (lag-1 ACF):       %.3f\n", rho_1))

# First significant lag in PACF
significant_pacf_lags <- which(abs(pacf_result$acf) > ci_level)
if (length(significant_pacf_lags) > 0) {
  cat(sprintf("  Significant PACF lags: %s\n", 
              paste(significant_pacf_lags, collapse = ", ")))
} else {
  cat("  No significant PACF lags detected\n")
}

# Check if lag-1 is significant
if (abs(rho_1) > ci_level) {
  cat(sprintf("  ✓ Lag-1 autocorrelation is SIGNIFICANT (|ρ₁| > %.4f)\n", ci_level))
  cat("  → This confirms the need for autocorrelation-corrected tests\n\n")
} else {
  cat(sprintf("  Lag-1 autocorrelation is NOT significant (|ρ₁| ≤ %.4f)\n\n", ci_level))
}

# Effective sample size calculation
rho_k <- acf_result$acf[-1][1:min(24, length(acf_result$acf[-1]))]
k <- 1:length(rho_k)
neff <- n / (1 + 2 * sum((1 - k/n) * rho_k))

cat(sprintf("Effective Sample Size:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  Original N:           %d\n", n))
cat(sprintf("  Effective N:          %.1f\n", neff))
cat(sprintf("  Reduction:            %.1f%%\n\n", 100 * (1 - neff/n)))

# ============================================================================
# STEP 3: CREATE COMBINED ACF/PACF PLOT
# ============================================================================

cat("Creating combined ACF/PACF plot...\n")

# Open PNG device
output_file <- file.path(plot_dir, "Fig_ACF_PACF_Analysis.png")
png(filename = output_file, 
    width = 12, height = 10, units = "in", res = 300,
    bg = "white")

# Set up 2-row layout with margins
par(mfrow = c(2, 1),
    mar = c(4, 4.5, 3.5, 2),  # bottom, left, top, right margins
    oma = c(2, 0, 3, 0),       # outer margins for main title
    bg = "#FFF9F0")            # Beige background

# --- PANEL A: ACF PLOT ---
plot(acf_result, 
     main = "",
     xlab = "Lag (months)",
     ylab = "Autocorrelation",
     las = 1,              # Horizontal axis labels
     lwd = 2,              # Line width for bars
     ci.col = "#1F77B4",   # Color for confidence interval
     col = "gray30")       # Color for bars

# Add panel label
mtext("A. Autocorrelation Function (ACF)", 
      side = 3, line = 2.2, adj = 0, font = 2, cex = 1.1)

# Add subtitle with rho_1 value using expression for proper Greek letter and subscript
mtext(bquote("Lag-1 autocorrelation: " * rho[1] * " = " * .(sprintf("%.3f", rho_1))),
      side = 3, line = 0.8, adj = 0, font = 1, cex = 0.9, col = "gray30")

# Add CI annotation
text(x = max_lag * 0.05, y = 0.95, 
     labels = sprintf("95%% CI: ±%.3f", ci_level),
     pos = 4, col = "#1F77B4", font = 3, cex = 0.9)

# --- PANEL B: PACF PLOT ---
plot(pacf_result,
     main = "",
     xlab = "Lag (months)",
     ylab = "Partial Autocorrelation",
     las = 1,
     lwd = 2,
     ci.col = "#1F77B4",
     col = "gray30")

# Add panel label
mtext("B. Partial Autocorrelation Function (PACF)", 
      side = 3, line = 2.2, adj = 0, font = 2, cex = 1.1)

# Add subtitle with AR model suggestion
ar_order <- ifelse(length(significant_pacf_lags) > 0, 
                   max(significant_pacf_lags), 0)
mtext(sprintf("Suggests AR(%d) model structure", ar_order),
      side = 3, line = 0.8, adj = 0, font = 1, cex = 0.9, col = "gray30")

# Add CI annotation
text(x = max_lag * 0.05, y = max(pacf_result$acf) * 0.9, 
     labels = sprintf("95%% CI: ±%.3f", ci_level),
     pos = 4, col = "#1F77B4", font = 3, cex = 0.9)

# --- ADD OVERALL TITLE AND CAPTION ---
mtext("Temporal Autocorrelation Structure: Pan-Arctic Storminess Index (1958–2024)",
      side = 3, line = 0.5, outer = TRUE, font = 2, cex = 1.3)

# Use expression for subscript in caption
mtext(bquote("Red points indicate significant autocorrelation at " * alpha * " = 0.05 | n = " * 
             .(n) * ", " * n[eff] * " = " * .(sprintf("%.0f", neff)) * 
             " (" * .(sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * (1 - neff/n))) * " reduction)"),
      side = 1, line = 0.5, outer = TRUE, font = 1, cex = 0.8, col = "gray40")

# Close device
dev.off()

cat(sprintf("  ✓ ACF/PACF plot saved: %s\n\n", basename(output_file)))

# ============================================================================
# STEP 4: CREATE ACF TABLE FOR FIRST 12 LAGS
# ============================================================================

cat("ACF Values for First 12 Lags:\n")
cat(rep("-", 50), "\n")
cat("Lag | ACF Value | Significant?\n")
cat(rep("-", 50), "\n")

for (i in 2:min(13, length(acf_result$acf))) {  # Start from 2 to skip lag 0
  lag_num <- i - 1
  acf_val <- acf_result$acf[i]
  sig_flag <- ifelse(abs(acf_val) > ci_level, "***", "")
  cat(sprintf("%3d | %9.4f | %s\n", lag_num, acf_val, sig_flag))
}
cat("\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 5: SUMMARY AND INTERPRETATION
# ============================================================================

cat(rep("=", 80), "\n")
cat("ACF/PACF ANALYSIS COMPLETE\n")
cat(rep("=", 80), "\n\n")

cat("Key Findings:\n")
cat(rep("-", 50), "\n")
cat(sprintf("1. Lag-1 Autocorrelation: ρ₁ = %.3f\n", rho_1))
if (abs(rho_1) > 0.1) {
  cat("   → STRONG persistence detected (|ρ₁| > 0.1)\n")
  cat("   → Violates independence assumption of standard tests\n")
}
cat(sprintf("\n2. Effective Sample Size: %.0f (%.1f%% of original)\n", 
            neff, 100 * neff/n))
cat("   → Autocorrelation reduces statistical degrees of freedom\n")

cat(sprintf("\n3. PACF Significant Lags: %s\n", 
            ifelse(length(significant_pacf_lags) > 0,
                   paste(significant_pacf_lags, collapse = ", "),
                   "None")))

cat("\n4. Implications for Trend Analysis:\n")
cat("   ✓ Pre-Whitened Mann-Kendall test (autocorrelation-aware) is REQUIRED\n")
cat("   ✓ Block bootstrap should use appropriate block length\n")
cat("   ✓ Standard OLS regression would yield inflated significance\n")

cat("\n\nGenerated File:\n")
cat(sprintf("  %s\n\n", basename(output_file)))

cat("Interpretation Guide:\n")
cat("  • ACF shows ALL correlations (direct + indirect effects)\n")
cat("  • PACF shows DIRECT correlations (removing intermediate effects)\n")
cat("  • Significant lag-1 PACF suggests AR(1) process\n")
cat("  • Multiple significant PACF lags suggest higher-order AR(p) process\n")
cat("  • Slow ACF decay indicates long-range persistence\n\n")

cat(rep("=", 80), "\n")
```

```{r distribution-normality}
# ============================================================================
# PHASE 1: DISTRIBUTION AND NORMALITY ASSESSMENT
# Pan-Arctic Storminess Index (1958-2024)
# ============================================================================
#
# PURPOSE: Assess the statistical distribution of the storminess index:
#   - Histogram with fitted normal distribution
#   - Q-Q plot to check normality assumption
#   - Box plots by decade to detect temporal changes in distribution
#   - Summary statistics
#
# INTERPRETATION:
#   - Informs choice of parametric vs non-parametric tests
#   - Identifies outliers and extreme values
#   - Assesses homogeneity of variance over time
#
# INPUT: Requires 'storm_df' data frame with columns: date, storminess
# ============================================================================

# --- SETUP ---
plot_dir <- here("Plots", "phase1_diagnostics")
if (!dir.exists(plot_dir)) dir.create(plot_dir, recursive = TRUE)

cat("\n", rep("=", 80), "\n")
cat("PHASE 1: DISTRIBUTION AND NORMALITY ASSESSMENT\n")
cat(rep("=", 80), "\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 1: CALCULATE DISTRIBUTION STATISTICS
# ============================================================================

cat("Calculating distribution statistics...\n")

# Basic statistics
mean_val <- mean(storm_df$storminess, na.rm = TRUE)
median_val <- median(storm_df$storminess, na.rm = TRUE)
sd_val <- sd(storm_df$storminess, na.rm = TRUE)
min_val <- min(storm_df$storminess, na.rm = TRUE)
max_val <- max(storm_df$storminess, na.rm = TRUE)

# Skewness and Kurtosis
# Skewness: measure of asymmetry (0 = symmetric, >0 = right skew, <0 = left skew)
# Kurtosis: measure of tail heaviness (3 = normal, >3 = heavy tails, <3 = light tails)
n <- length(storm_df$storminess)
skewness <- (1/n) * sum((storm_df$storminess - mean_val)^3) / sd_val^3
kurtosis <- (1/n) * sum((storm_df$storminess - mean_val)^4) / sd_val^4

# Excess kurtosis (subtract 3 to compare with normal distribution)
excess_kurtosis <- kurtosis - 3

# Quartiles
q1 <- quantile(storm_df$storminess, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
q3 <- quantile(storm_df$storminess, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
iqr <- q3 - q1

# Shapiro-Wilk test for normality (if n < 5000)
if (n < 5000) {
  shapiro_test <- shapiro.test(storm_df$storminess)
  shapiro_p <- shapiro_test$p.value
  shapiro_w <- shapiro_test$statistic
} else {
  # For large samples, use Kolmogorov-Smirnov test
  ks_test <- ks.test(storm_df$storminess, "pnorm", mean_val, sd_val)
  shapiro_p <- ks_test$p.value
  shapiro_w <- ks_test$statistic
}

cat(sprintf("  Mean:             %.2f m⁴/s⁴\n", mean_val))
cat(sprintf("  Median:           %.2f m⁴/s⁴\n", median_val))
cat(sprintf("  Std. Deviation:   %.2f m⁴/s⁴\n", sd_val))
cat(sprintf("  Skewness:         %.3f\n", skewness))
cat(sprintf("  Excess Kurtosis:  %.3f\n", excess_kurtosis))
cat(sprintf("  Shapiro-Wilk W:   %.4f (p = %.4f)\n\n", shapiro_w, shapiro_p))

if (shapiro_p < 0.05) {
  cat("  → Data significantly deviates from normality (p < 0.05)\n")
  cat("  → Non-parametric methods are appropriate\n\n")
} else {
  cat("  → Data does not significantly deviate from normality (p ≥ 0.05)\n\n")
}

# ============================================================================
# STEP 2: PREPARE DATA BY DECADE
# ============================================================================

cat("Preparing decadal breakdown...\n")

# Add decade column
storm_df <- storm_df %>%
  mutate(
    decade = floor(year(date) / 10) * 10,
    decade_label = paste0(decade, "s")
  )

# Count observations per decade
decade_counts <- storm_df %>%
  group_by(decade_label) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop")

cat("  Observations per decade:\n")
for (i in 1:nrow(decade_counts)) {
  cat(sprintf("    %s: %d months\n", decade_counts$decade_label[i], decade_counts$n[i]))
}
cat("\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 3: CREATE FOUR-PANEL DIAGNOSTIC PLOT
# ============================================================================

cat("Creating distribution diagnostic plots...\n")

# Common theme
common_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", hjust = 0),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 9),
    panel.grid.minor = element_line(linewidth = 0.2, color = "gray90"),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(linewidth = 0.3, color = "gray85"),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#FFF9F0", color = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10)
  )

# --- PANEL A: HISTOGRAM WITH NORMAL CURVE ---
p1 <- ggplot(storm_df, aes(x = storminess)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), 
                 bins = 40, fill = "gray60", color = "gray30", alpha = 0.7) +
  stat_function(fun = dnorm, 
                args = list(mean = mean_val, sd = sd_val),
                color = "#D62728", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean_val, linetype = "dashed", 
             color = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = median_val, linetype = "dotted", 
             color = "#1F77B4", linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = "A. Histogram with Normal Distribution",
    subtitle = sprintf("Skewness = %.3f, Excess Kurtosis = %.3f", 
                      skewness, excess_kurtosis),
    x = expression(paste("Storminess Index (m"^4, " s"^{-4}, ")")),
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  common_theme +
  annotate("text", x = mean_val, y = Inf, 
           label = "Mean", vjust = 1.5, hjust = -0.1, size = 3, fontface = "bold") +
  annotate("text", x = median_val, y = Inf, 
           label = "Median", vjust = 1.5, hjust = 1.1, size = 3, 
           fontface = "bold", color = "#1F77B4")

# --- PANEL B: Q-Q PLOT ---
# Calculate theoretical quantiles
theoretical_q <- qnorm(ppoints(length(storm_df$storminess)))
sample_q <- sort(storm_df$storminess)

qq_df <- data.frame(
  theoretical = theoretical_q,
  sample = sample_q
)

p2 <- ggplot(qq_df, aes(x = theoretical, y = sample)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1.5, color = "gray40") +
  geom_abline(intercept = mean_val, slope = sd_val, 
              color = "#D62728", linewidth = 1.2) +
  labs(
    title = "B. Q-Q Plot (Normal Distribution)",
    subtitle = sprintf("Shapiro-Wilk W = %.4f, p = %.4f", shapiro_w, shapiro_p),
    x = "Theoretical Quantiles",
    y = "Sample Quantiles"
  ) +
  common_theme

# --- PANEL C: BOX PLOTS BY DECADE ---
p3 <- ggplot(storm_df, aes(x = decade_label, y = storminess)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "gray70", color = "gray30", alpha = 0.7,
               outlier.color = "#D62728", outlier.size = 2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean_val, linetype = "dashed", 
             color = "black", linewidth = 0.7) +
  labs(
    title = "C. Distribution by Decade",
    subtitle = "Red points indicate outliers (> 1.5 × IQR from quartiles)",
    x = "Decade",
    y = expression(paste("Storminess Index (m"^4, " s"^{-4}, ")"))
  ) +
  common_theme +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# --- PANEL D: VARIANCE OVER TIME (ROLLING WINDOW) ---
# Calculate rolling standard deviation (24-month window)
storm_df <- storm_df %>%
  arrange(date) %>%
  mutate(
    rolling_sd = zoo::rollapply(storminess, width = 24, FUN = sd, 
                                fill = NA, align = "center")
  )

p4 <- ggplot(storm_df, aes(x = date, y = rolling_sd)) +
  geom_line(color = "#1F77B4", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = sd_val, linetype = "dashed", 
             color = "black", linewidth = 0.7) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "10 years", date_labels = "%Y") +
  labs(
    title = "D. Temporal Variability (24-month Rolling Std. Dev.)",
    subtitle = "Assesses homogeneity of variance over time",
    x = "Year",
    y = expression(paste("Rolling Std. Dev. (m"^4, " s"^{-4}, ")"))
  ) +
  common_theme

# --- COMBINE ALL PANELS ---
combined_plot <- grid.arrange(
  p1, p2, p3, p4,
  ncol = 2,
  top = grid::textGrob(
    "Distribution and Normality Assessment: Pan-Arctic Storminess Index (1958–2024)",
    gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 15, fontface = "bold")
  ),
  bottom = grid::textGrob(
    sprintf("n = %d | Mean = %.2f | SD = %.2f | Skewness = %.3f | Excess Kurtosis = %.3f",
            n, mean_val, sd_val, skewness, excess_kurtosis),
    gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 9, col = "gray40")
  )
)

# ============================================================================
# STEP 4: SAVE PLOT
# ============================================================================

output_file <- file.path(plot_dir, "Fig_Distribution_Normality_Assessment.png")

ggsave(
  filename = output_file,
  plot = combined_plot,
  width = 14,
  height = 11,
  dpi = 300,
  bg = "white"
)

cat(sprintf("  ✓ Distribution assessment plot saved: %s\n\n", basename(output_file)))

# ============================================================================
# STEP 5: IDENTIFY AND REPORT OUTLIERS
# ============================================================================

cat("Outlier Analysis:\n")
cat(rep("-", 50), "\n")

# Define outliers using IQR method
lower_fence <- q1 - 1.5 * iqr
upper_fence <- q3 + 1.5 * iqr

outliers <- storm_df %>%
  filter(storminess < lower_fence | storminess > upper_fence) %>%
  select(date, storminess) %>%
  arrange(desc(storminess))

cat(sprintf("  Lower fence (Q1 - 1.5×IQR): %.2f\n", lower_fence))
cat(sprintf("  Upper fence (Q3 + 1.5×IQR): %.2f\n", upper_fence))
cat(sprintf("  Number of outliers: %d (%.1f%% of data)\n\n", 
            nrow(outliers), 100 * nrow(outliers) / n))

if (nrow(outliers) > 0) {
  cat("  Top 10 extreme values:\n")
  for (i in 1:min(10, nrow(outliers))) {
    cat(sprintf("    %s: %.2f m⁴/s⁴\n", 
                format(outliers$date[i], "%Y-%m-%d"), 
                outliers$storminess[i]))
  }
  cat("\n")
}

# ============================================================================
# STEP 6: SUMMARY AND INTERPRETATION
# ============================================================================

cat(rep("=", 80), "\n")
cat("DISTRIBUTION ASSESSMENT COMPLETE\n")
cat(rep("=", 80), "\n\n")

cat("Key Findings:\n")
cat(rep("-", 50), "\n")

cat(sprintf("1. Central Tendency:\n"))
cat(sprintf("   Mean = %.2f m⁴/s⁴, Median = %.2f m⁴/s⁴\n", mean_val, median_val))
if (abs(mean_val - median_val) / sd_val > 0.1) {
  cat("   → Noticeable difference suggests asymmetry\n")
} else {
  cat("   → Mean ≈ Median suggests symmetric distribution\n")
}

cat(sprintf("\n2. Distribution Shape:\n"))
if (abs(skewness) < 0.5) {
  cat(sprintf("   Skewness = %.3f → Approximately symmetric\n", skewness))
} else if (skewness > 0) {
  cat(sprintf("   Skewness = %.3f → Positively skewed (right tail)\n", skewness))
} else {
  cat(sprintf("   Skewness = %.3f → Negatively skewed (left tail)\n", skewness))
}

if (abs(excess_kurtosis) < 0.5) {
  cat(sprintf("   Excess Kurtosis = %.3f → Normal tail behavior\n", excess_kurtosis))
} else if (excess_kurtosis > 0) {
  cat(sprintf("   Excess Kurtosis = %.3f → Heavy tails (more extremes)\n", excess_kurtosis))
} else {
  cat(sprintf("   Excess Kurtosis = %.3f → Light tails (fewer extremes)\n", excess_kurtosis))
}

cat(sprintf("\n3. Normality Test:\n"))
cat(sprintf("   Shapiro-Wilk W = %.4f, p-value = %.4f\n", shapiro_w, shapiro_p))
if (shapiro_p < 0.05) {
  cat("   → REJECT null hypothesis of normality (p < 0.05)\n")
  cat("   → Data is NOT normally distributed\n")
  cat("   → Non-parametric tests (Mann-Kendall) are appropriate\n")
} else {
  cat("   → FAIL TO REJECT null hypothesis (p ≥ 0.05)\n")
  cat("   → Data approximates normal distribution\n")
}

cat(sprintf("\n4. Temporal Homogeneity:\n"))
cat("   Check Panel D for variance changes over time\n")
cat("   → Stable variance supports stationarity assumption\n")
cat("   → Increasing variance may indicate heteroscedasticity\n")

cat("\n\nGenerated File:\n")
cat(sprintf("  %s\n\n", basename(output_file)))

cat("Interpretation Guide:\n")
cat("  Panel A: Shows overall distribution shape vs. normal curve\n")
cat("  Panel B: Deviations from diagonal indicate non-normality\n")
cat("  Panel C: Compares distributions across decades\n")
cat("  Panel D: Assesses if variability changes over time\n\n")

cat(rep("=", 80), "\n")
```

```{r monthly-climatology}
# ============================================================================
# PHASE 1: MONTHLY CLIMATOLOGY - MEAN ANNUAL CYCLE
# Pan-Arctic Storminess Index (1958-2024)
# ============================================================================
#
# PURPOSE: Characterize the climatological mean annual cycle:
#   - Mean storminess for each calendar month
#   - Variability within each month (error bars)
#   - Peak and trough identification
#   - Seasonal patterns
#
# This establishes the baseline seasonal cycle against which 
# all subsequent analyses are compared.
#
# INPUT: Requires 'storm_df' data frame with columns: date, storminess
# ============================================================================

# --- SETUP ---
plot_dir <- here("Plots", "phase1_diagnostics")
if (!dir.exists(plot_dir)) dir.create(plot_dir, recursive = TRUE)

cat("\n", rep("=", 80), "\n")
cat("PHASE 1: MONTHLY CLIMATOLOGY - MEAN ANNUAL CYCLE\n")
cat(rep("=", 80), "\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 1: CALCULATE MONTHLY CLIMATOLOGY
# ============================================================================

cat("Calculating monthly climatological statistics...\n")

# Calculate statistics for each calendar month
monthly_clim <- storm_df %>%
  mutate(month = month(date, label = TRUE, abbr = TRUE)) %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = mean(storminess, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(storminess, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(storminess, na.rm = TRUE),
    se = sd / sqrt(n()),  # Standard error
    q25 = quantile(storminess, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q75 = quantile(storminess, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    min = min(storminess, na.rm = TRUE),
    max = max(storminess, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    month_num = as.numeric(month),
    ci_lower = mean - 1.96 * se,  # 95% CI
    ci_upper = mean + 1.96 * se
  )

# Identify peak and trough months
peak_month <- monthly_clim$month[which.max(monthly_clim$mean)]
peak_value <- max(monthly_clim$mean)
trough_month <- monthly_clim$month[which.min(monthly_clim$mean)]
trough_value <- min(monthly_clim$mean)
annual_range <- peak_value - trough_value

cat("\nMonthly Climatology Statistics:\n")
cat(rep("-", 70), "\n")
cat(sprintf("%-5s | %8s | %8s | %8s | %8s | %s\n", 
            "Month", "Mean", "Median", "Std Dev", "Range", "N"))
cat(rep("-", 70), "\n")

for (i in 1:nrow(monthly_clim)) {
  cat(sprintf("%-5s | %8.2f | %8.2f | %8.2f | %8.2f | %d\n",
              monthly_clim$month[i],
              monthly_clim$mean[i],
              monthly_clim$median[i],
              monthly_clim$sd[i],
              monthly_clim$max[i] - monthly_clim$min[i],
              monthly_clim$n[i]))
}

cat(rep("-", 70), "\n\n")

cat(sprintf("Key Findings:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  Peak month:        %s (%.2f m⁴/s⁴)\n", peak_month, peak_value))
cat(sprintf("  Trough month:      %s (%.2f m⁴/s⁴)\n", trough_month, trough_value))
cat(sprintf("  Annual amplitude:  %.2f m⁴/s⁴ (%.1f%% of annual mean)\n\n", 
            annual_range, 100 * annual_range / mean(storm_df$storminess)))

# Identify seasonal patterns
winter_months <- c("Dec", "Jan", "Feb")
spring_months <- c("Mar", "Apr", "May")
summer_months <- c("Jun", "Jul", "Aug")
autumn_months <- c("Sep", "Oct", "Nov")

winter_mean <- mean(monthly_clim$mean[monthly_clim$month %in% winter_months])
spring_mean <- mean(monthly_clim$mean[monthly_clim$month %in% spring_months])
summer_mean <- mean(monthly_clim$mean[monthly_clim$month %in% summer_months])
autumn_mean <- mean(monthly_clim$mean[monthly_clim$month %in% autumn_months])

cat("Seasonal Averages:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Winter (DJF):  %.2f m⁴/s⁴\n", winter_mean))
cat(sprintf("  Spring (MAM):  %.2f m⁴/s⁴\n", spring_mean))
cat(sprintf("  Summer (JJA):  %.2f m⁴/s⁴\n", summer_mean))
cat(sprintf("  Autumn (SON):  %.2f m⁴/s⁴\n\n", autumn_mean))

# ============================================================================
# STEP 2: CREATE MAIN CLIMATOLOGY PLOT
# ============================================================================

cat("Creating monthly climatology plot...\n")

p_main <- ggplot(monthly_clim, aes(x = month, y = mean, group = 1)) +
  
  # Shaded seasonal backgrounds
  annotate("rect", xmin = 0.5, xmax = 3.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = "#E3F2FD", alpha = 0.3) +  # Winter (Dec-Feb)
  annotate("rect", xmin = 3.5, xmax = 6.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = "#F1F8E9", alpha = 0.3) +  # Spring (Mar-May)
  annotate("rect", xmin = 6.5, xmax = 9.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = "#FFF9C4", alpha = 0.3) +  # Summer (Jun-Aug)
  annotate("rect", xmin = 9.5, xmax = 12.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = "#FFE0B2", alpha = 0.3) +  # Autumn (Sep-Nov)
  
  # Error bars (95% CI)
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper), 
                width = 0.3, color = "gray40", linewidth = 0.6) +
  
  # Connect months with line
  geom_line(color = "#1F77B4", linewidth = 1.3) +
  
  # Points for each month
  geom_point(size = 4, color = "#1F77B4", fill = "#1F77B4", shape = 21) +
  
  # Highlight peak month
  geom_point(data = subset(monthly_clim, month == peak_month),
             size = 5, color = "#D62728", shape = 17) +
  
  # Highlight trough month
  geom_point(data = subset(monthly_clim, month == trough_month),
             size = 5, color = "#2CA02C", shape = 17) +
  
  # Horizontal line at annual mean
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(storm_df$storminess), 
             linetype = "dashed", color = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
  
  # Labels and scales
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, ceiling(max(monthly_clim$ci_upper)/20)*20, by = 20),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.08))
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Mean Annual Cycle of Arctic Storminess (1958–2024)",
    subtitle = sprintf("Peak: %s (%.1f m⁴ s⁻⁴) | Trough: %s (%.1f m⁴ s⁻⁴) | Amplitude: %.1f m⁴ s⁻⁴",
                      peak_month, peak_value, trough_month, trough_value, annual_range),
    x = "Month",
    y = expression(paste("Mean Storminess Index (m"^4, " s"^{-4}, ")"))
  ) +
  
  # Theme
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, 
                              margin = margin(b = 5)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, hjust = 0.5, 
                                 margin = margin(b = 15), color = "gray30"),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", margin = margin(t = 10)),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", margin = margin(r = 10)),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(linewidth = 0.4, color = "gray85"),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#FFF9F0", color = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.margin = margin(15, 15, 15, 15)
  ) +
  
  # Annotations for peak and trough
  annotate("text", x = which(monthly_clim$month == peak_month), 
           y = peak_value + annual_range * 0.15,
           label = "Peak", color = "#D62728", fontface = "bold", size = 4) +
  
  annotate("text", x = which(monthly_clim$month == trough_month), 
           y = trough_value - annual_range * 0.15,
           label = "Trough", color = "#2CA02C", fontface = "bold", size = 4) +
  
  # Season labels
  annotate("text", x = 2, y = Inf, label = "Winter", 
           vjust = 1.5, size = 3.5, fontface = "italic", color = "#1565C0") +
  annotate("text", x = 5, y = Inf, label = "Spring", 
           vjust = 1.5, size = 3.5, fontface = "italic", color = "#558B2F") +
  annotate("text", x = 8, y = Inf, label = "Summer", 
           vjust = 1.5, size = 3.5, fontface = "italic", color = "#F9A825") +
  annotate("text", x = 11, y = Inf, label = "Autumn", 
           vjust = 1.5, size = 3.5, fontface = "italic", color = "#EF6C00") +
  
  # Legend for error bars
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = min(monthly_clim$ci_lower) + annual_range * 0.05,
           label = "Error bars: 95% CI", hjust = 0, size = 3, 
           color = "gray40", fontface = "italic")

p_main <- p_main +
  annotate("text", 
           x = 12.5, 
           y = mean(storm_df$storminess) + 3,  # Slightly above the line
           label = sprintf("Annual mean: %.1f m⁴/s⁴", mean(storm_df$storminess)),
           hjust = 1, size = 3.5, color = "black", fontface = "italic")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 3: SAVE MAIN PLOT
# ============================================================================

output_file <- file.path(plot_dir, "Fig_Monthly_Climatology.png")

ggsave(
  filename = output_file,
  plot = p_main,
  width = 14,
  height = 8,
  dpi = 300,
  bg = "white"
)

cat(sprintf("  ✓ Monthly climatology plot saved: %s\n\n", basename(output_file)))

# ============================================================================
# STEP 4: CREATE SUPPLEMENTARY VARIABILITY PLOT
# ============================================================================

cat("Creating supplementary variability plot...\n")

p_variability <- ggplot(monthly_clim, aes(x = month, y = sd, group = 1)) +
  
  # Seasonal backgrounds (same as main plot)
  annotate("rect", xmin = 0.5, xmax = 3.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = "#E3F2FD", alpha = 0.3) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 3.5, xmax = 6.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = "#F1F8E9", alpha = 0.3) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 6.5, xmax = 9.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = "#FFF9C4", alpha = 0.3) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 9.5, xmax = 12.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = "#FFE0B2", alpha = 0.3) +
  
  # Bar plot
  geom_col(fill = "#1F77B4", alpha = 0.7, color = "gray30", linewidth = 0.3) +
  
  # Line connecting tops
  geom_line(color = "#D62728", linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(color = "#D62728", size = 3) +
  
  # Mean line
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(monthly_clim$sd), 
             linetype = "dashed", color = "black", linewidth = 0.7) +
  
  # Annotation for mean SD line
  annotate("text", 
           x = 12.5, 
           y = mean(monthly_clim$sd) + 2,
           label = sprintf("Mean SD: %.1f m⁴/s⁴", mean(monthly_clim$sd)),
           hjust = 1, size = 3.5, color = "black", fontface = "italic") +
  
  labs(
    title = "Monthly Variability of Arctic Storminess (1958–2024)",
    subtitle = "Standard deviation shows month-to-month consistency",
    x = "Month",
    y = z
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, 
                              margin = margin(b = 5)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, hjust = 0.5, 
                                 margin = margin(b = 15), color = "gray30"),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", margin = margin(t = 10)),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", margin = margin(r = 10)),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 11),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(linewidth = 0.4, color = "gray85"),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#FFF9F0", color = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.margin = margin(15, 15, 15, 15)
  )

output_file_var <- file.path(plot_dir, "Fig_Monthly_Variability.png")

ggsave(
  filename = output_file_var,
  plot = p_variability,
  width = 14,
  height = 7,
  dpi = 300,
  bg = "white"
)

# ============================================================================
# STEP 5: SUMMARY AND INTERPRETATION
# ============================================================================

cat(rep("=", 80), "\n")
cat("MONTHLY CLIMATOLOGY ANALYSIS COMPLETE\n")
cat(rep("=", 80), "\n\n")

cat("Key Findings:\n")
cat(rep("-", 50), "\n")

cat(sprintf("1. Annual Cycle Characteristics:\n"))
cat(sprintf("   Peak month:     %s (%.2f m⁴/s⁴)\n", peak_month, peak_value))
cat(sprintf("   Trough month:   %s (%.2f m⁴/s⁴)\n", trough_month, trough_value))
cat(sprintf("   Amplitude:      %.2f m⁴/s⁴ (%.1f%% of mean)\n\n", 
            annual_range, 100 * annual_range / mean(storm_df$storminess)))

cat("2. Seasonal Pattern:\n")
if (winter_mean == max(c(winter_mean, spring_mean, summer_mean, autumn_mean))) {
  cat("   → Winter is the stormiest season\n")
} else if (autumn_mean == max(c(winter_mean, spring_mean, summer_mean, autumn_mean))) {
  cat("   → Autumn is the stormiest season\n")
}
if (summer_mean == min(c(winter_mean, spring_mean, summer_mean, autumn_mean))) {
  cat("   → Summer is the quietest season\n")
}

cat("\n3. Variability Pattern:\n")
max_sd_month <- monthly_clim$month[which.max(monthly_clim$sd)]
min_sd_month <- monthly_clim$month[which.min(monthly_clim$sd)]
cat(sprintf("   Highest variability: %s (σ = %.2f)\n", 
            max_sd_month, max(monthly_clim$sd)))
cat(sprintf("   Lowest variability:  %s (σ = %.2f)\n", 
            min_sd_month, min(monthly_clim$sd)))

cat("\n\nGenerated Files:\n")
cat(sprintf("  1. %s (main climatology)\n", basename(output_file)))
cat(sprintf("  2. %s (variability)\n\n", basename(output_file_var)))

cat("Interpretation Notes:\n")
cat("  • Strong annual cycle indicates seasonal forcing mechanisms\n")
cat("  • Peak in winter/autumn suggests extratropical cyclone dominance\n")
cat("  • Error bars show 95% confidence intervals for each month\n")
cat("  • Higher winter variability reflects more variable storm activity\n\n")

cat(rep("=", 80), "\n")
```

```{r storminess-index-climatological-maps}
# ============================================================================
# PHASE 1: STORMINESS INDEX CLIMATOLOGICAL MAPS
#
# PURPOSE: Create polar projection maps showing the long-term mean
#          spatial distribution of the storminess index
#   Figure 1: Annual Mean
#   Figure 2: Seasonal Means (DJF, MAM, JJA, SON)
#
# This completes Section 1.2: Characterization of the Mean State
# ============================================================================

# --- SETUP ---
processed_dir <- here("data", "processed")
plot_dir <- here("Plots", "phase1_diagnostics")
if (!dir.exists(plot_dir)) dir.create(plot_dir, recursive = TRUE)

cat("\n", rep("=", 80), "\n")
cat("PHASE 1: STORMINESS INDEX CLIMATOLOGICAL MAPS\n")
cat(rep("=", 80), "\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# DEFINE SEASONS
# ============================================================================

season_definitions <- list(
  Annual = list(months = 1:12, name = "Annual Mean", abbr = "ANN", label = "Annual Mean"),
  DJF = list(months = c(12, 1, 2), name = "Winter", abbr = "DJF", label = "Winter (DJF)"),
  MAM = list(months = c(3, 4, 5), name = "Spring", abbr = "MAM", label = "Spring (MAM)"),
  JJA = list(months = c(6, 7, 8), name = "Summer", abbr = "JJA", label = "Summer (JJA)"),
  SON = list(months = c(9, 10, 11), name = "Autumn", abbr = "SON", label = "Autumn (SON)")
)

# ============================================================================
# LOAD STORMINESS INDEX DATA
# ============================================================================

cat("Loading storminess index NetCDF data...\n")

nc_storm <- nc_open(file.path(processed_dir, "ERA5_storminess_index_monthly_1958-2024.nc"))

storminess <- ncvar_get(nc_storm, "storminess_index")
lat <- ncvar_get(nc_storm, "latitude")
lon <- ncvar_get(nc_storm, "longitude")

nc_close(nc_storm)

# Check and fix dimension order
cat(sprintf("  Original dimensions: [%s]\n", paste(dim(storminess), collapse = ", ")))

# Permute to [time, lat, lon] if needed
if (dim(storminess)[1] == length(lon)) {
  cat("  Permuting dimensions to [time, lat, lon]...\n")
  storminess <- aperm(storminess, c(3, 2, 1))
}

n_times <- dim(storminess)[1]
dates <- seq(as.Date("1958-01-01"), by = "month", length.out = n_times)

cat(sprintf("  Final dimensions: [%d times, %d lats, %d lons]\n", 
            dim(storminess)[1], dim(storminess)[2], dim(storminess)[3]))

# ============================================================================
# CALCULATE SEASONAL CLIMATOLOGIES
# ============================================================================

cat("\nCalculating seasonal climatologies...\n")

seasonal_data <- list()
all_values <- c()

for (season_name in names(season_definitions)) {
  months <- season_definitions[[season_name]]$months
  season_indices <- which(month(dates) %in% months)
  
  # Calculate mean across time for each grid point
  storm_season <- apply(storminess[season_indices, , ], c(2, 3), mean, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  seasonal_data[[season_name]] <- storm_season
  all_values <- c(all_values, as.vector(storm_season))
  
  cat(sprintf("  %s: Mean = %.2f, Range = [%.2f, %.2f] m⁴/s⁴\n",
              season_definitions[[season_name]]$label,
              mean(storm_season, na.rm = TRUE),
              min(storm_season, na.rm = TRUE),
              max(storm_season, na.rm = TRUE)))
}

# Calculate global range for uniform color scale
global_range <- range(all_values, na.rm = TRUE)
cat(sprintf("\n*** GLOBAL COLOR RANGE: %.1f to %.1f m⁴/s⁴ ***\n\n", 
            global_range[1], global_range[2]))

# ============================================================================
# PREPARE CARTOGRAPHIC ELEMENTS
# ============================================================================

cat("Preparing cartographic elements...\n")

arctic_crs <- "+proj=laea +lat_0=90 +lon_0=0"
view_radius <- 3700000
plot_radius <- 4400000

circle_mask <- st_sfc(st_point(c(0, 0)), crs = arctic_crs) %>%
  st_buffer(dist = view_radius)

square_box <- st_as_sfc(st_bbox(c(
  xmin = -plot_radius, xmax = plot_radius,
  ymin = -plot_radius, ymax = plot_radius
), crs = arctic_crs))
inverse_mask <- st_difference(square_box, circle_mask)

world <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")
world_polar <- st_transform(world, crs = arctic_crs)

graticules <- st_graticule(
  lon = seq(-180, 180, by = 60),
  lat = c(60, 70, 80),
  crs = 4326
) %>%
  st_transform(crs = arctic_crs)

lat_labels <- data.frame(lon = 180, lat = c(60, 70, 80)) %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) %>%
  st_transform(crs = arctic_crs)
lat_labels$label <- c("60°N", "70°N", "80°N")

lon_labels <- data.frame(lon = seq(0, 300, by = 60), lat = 54) %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) %>%
  st_transform(crs = arctic_crs)
lon_labels$label <- c("0°", "60°E", "120°E", "180°", "120°W", "60°W")

cat("  ✓ Cartographic elements prepared\n")

# --- FIX 1: Calculate percentile-based color limits ---
# Use 1st and 99th percentiles to avoid extreme value skewing
color_lower <- quantile(all_values, 0.01, na.rm = TRUE)
color_upper <- quantile(all_values, 0.99, na.rm = TRUE)

cat(sprintf("\n*** COLOR SCALE (1st-99th percentile): %.1f to %.1f m⁴/s⁴ ***\n", 
            color_lower, color_upper))
cat(sprintf("*** Full range was: %.1f to %.1f m⁴/s⁴ ***\n\n", 
            global_range[1], global_range[2]))

# ============================================================================
# FUNCTION: CREATE SINGLE MAP
# ============================================================================

create_storminess_map <- function(data_matrix, title, show_legend = TRUE) {
  
  # Create stars object
 lon_vec <- as.vector(lon)
  lat_vec <- as.vector(lat)
  
  data_list <- list(storminess = t(data_matrix))
  dims <- st_dimensions(x = lon_vec, y = lat_vec)
  
  clim_stars <- st_as_stars(data_list, dimensions = dims) %>%
    st_set_crs(4326)
  
  # Warp and mask
  clim_polar <- st_warp(clim_stars, crs = arctic_crs)
  clim_polar_masked <- clim_polar[circle_mask]
  
  # Create plot with PERCENTILE-BASED color scale
  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_stars(data = clim_polar_masked, aes(fill = storminess), na.rm = TRUE) +
    scale_fill_viridis(
      name = expression(paste("Storminess (m"^4, " s"^{-4}, ")")),
      option = "inferno",
      na.value = "transparent",
      limits = c(color_lower, color_upper),  # Use percentile limits
      oob = scales::squish,  # Squish values outside limits to the extremes
      breaks = pretty(c(color_lower, color_upper), n = 5),
      guide = if (show_legend) guide_colorbar(barwidth = 1, barheight = 12) else "none"
    ) +
    geom_sf(data = world_polar, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_sf(data = graticules, color = "gray50", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.25) +
    geom_sf(data = inverse_mask, fill = "white", color = NA) +
    geom_sf_text(data = lat_labels, aes(label = label), size = 3, color = "black", hjust = 1.2) +
    geom_sf_text(data = lon_labels, aes(label = label), size = 3, color = "black") +
    coord_sf(xlim = c(-plot_radius, plot_radius), 
             ylim = c(-plot_radius, plot_radius), expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = title) +
    theme_void(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = 14),
      legend.position = if (show_legend) "right" else "none",
      legend.key.width = unit(0.8, "cm"),
      legend.key.height = unit(2.5, "cm"),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "gray95", color = NA),
      plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5)
    )
  
  return(p)
}

# ============================================================================
# FIGURE 1: ANNUAL MEAN CLIMATOLOGY
# ============================================================================

cat("\n=== FIGURE 1: ANNUAL MEAN CLIMATOLOGY ===\n")

p_annual <- create_storminess_map(
  seasonal_data[["Annual"]], 
  "Annual Mean (1958–2024)"
)

fig1 <- p_annual +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Arctic Storminess Index Climatology: Annual Mean",
    subtitle = "Lambert Azimuthal Equal-Area Projection | Monthly variance of synoptic-scale EKE",
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5, color = "gray30")
    )
  )

output_file1 <- file.path(plot_dir, "Fig_Climatology_Storminess_Annual.png")
ggsave(output_file1, fig1, width = 10, height = 10, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
cat(sprintf("  ✓ Saved: %s\n", basename(output_file1)))

# ============================================================================
# FIGURE 2: SEASONAL CLIMATOLOGIES (4-PANEL)
# ============================================================================

cat("\n=== FIGURE 2: SEASONAL CLIMATOLOGIES ===\n")

# Create individual season maps
p_djf <- create_storminess_map(seasonal_data[["DJF"]], "Winter (DJF)", show_legend = FALSE)
p_mam <- create_storminess_map(seasonal_data[["MAM"]], "Spring (MAM)", show_legend = FALSE)
p_jja <- create_storminess_map(seasonal_data[["JJA"]], "Summer (JJA)", show_legend = FALSE)
p_son <- create_storminess_map(seasonal_data[["SON"]], "Autumn (SON)", show_legend = TRUE)

# Combine into 2x2 grid
fig2 <- (p_djf | p_mam) / (p_jja | p_son) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Arctic Storminess Index Climatology: Seasonal Means (1958–2024)",
    subtitle = "Lambert Azimuthal Equal-Area Projection | Uniform color scale across all seasons",
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5, color = "gray30")
    )
  )

output_file2 <- file.path(plot_dir, "Fig_Climatology_Storminess_Seasonal.png")
ggsave(output_file2, fig2, width = 16, height = 16, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
cat(sprintf("  ✓ Saved: %s\n", basename(output_file2)))

# ============================================================================
# SUMMARY
# ============================================================================

cat("\n", rep("=", 80), "\n")
cat("STORMINESS INDEX CLIMATOLOGY MAPS COMPLETE!\n")
cat(rep("=", 80), "\n\n")

cat("Generated Figures:\n")
cat(sprintf("  1. %s (Annual mean)\n", basename(output_file1)))
cat(sprintf("  2. %s (2×2 seasonal grid)\n", basename(output_file2)))
cat(sprintf("  3. %s (5-panel comparison)\n\n", basename(output_file3)))

cat("Climatology Statistics:\n")
cat(rep("-", 60), "\n")
for (season_name in names(season_definitions)) {
  data <- seasonal_data[[season_name]]
  cat(sprintf("  %-15s: Mean = %6.2f, SD = %6.2f m⁴/s⁴\n",
              season_definitions[[season_name]]$label,
              mean(data, na.rm = TRUE),
              sd(data, na.rm = TRUE)))
}

cat(sprintf("\nGlobal color range: %.1f to %.1f m⁴/s⁴\n\n", 
            global_range[1], global_range[2]))

cat("Key Features:\n")
cat("  ✓ Uniform color scale across all maps for direct comparison\n")
cat("  ✓ Lambert Azimuthal Equal-Area projection (preserves area)\n")
cat("  ✓ Shows WHERE storminess is highest/lowest on average\n")
cat("  ✓ Seasonal differences clearly visible\n\n")

cat("Interpretation Guide:\n")
cat("  • High values (yellow/white): Regions of intense storm activity\n")
cat("  • Low values (dark): Regions of weak storm activity\n")
cat("  • Compare DJF vs SON for winter-autumn differences\n")
cat("  • Note the North Atlantic storm track pathway\n\n")

cat(rep("=", 80), "\n")
```

```{r}
# ============================================================================
# PHASE 1 DIAGNOSTICS FOR ALL REGIONAL SUB-ANALYSES
# Processes: Fram Strait AND Svalbard-Barents
# ============================================================================
#
# PURPOSE: Apply the full Phase 1 diagnostic suite to regional time series:
#   1. Primary Time Series Visualization
#   2. ACF/PACF Analysis
#   3. Distribution Assessment
#   4. Monthly Climatology
#
# PREREQUISITES: 
#   - Storminess NetCDF file loaded
#   - dates vector available (804 months)
# ============================================================================

# ============================================================================
# STEP 0: LOAD STORMINESS DATA (if not already loaded)
# ============================================================================

cat("\n", rep("=", 80), "\n")
cat("LOADING STORMINESS DATA\n")
cat(rep("=", 80), "\n\n")

# Load NetCDF data
processed_dir <- "E:/ERA5_data/processed"
nc_storm <- nc_open(file.path(processed_dir, "ERA5_storminess_index_monthly_1958-2024.nc"))

storminess <- ncvar_get(nc_storm, "storminess_index")
lat <- ncvar_get(nc_storm, "latitude")
lon <- ncvar_get(nc_storm, "longitude")

nc_close(nc_storm)

# Check and fix dimension order - should be [time, lat, lon]
if (dim(storminess)[1] == length(lon)) {
  cat("Permuting dimensions to [time, lat, lon]...\n")
  storminess <- aperm(storminess, c(3, 2, 1))
}

n_times <- dim(storminess)[1]
dates <- seq(as.Date("1958-01-01"), by = "month", length.out = n_times)

cat(sprintf("Data loaded: [%d times, %d lats, %d lons]\n\n", 
            dim(storminess)[1], dim(storminess)[2], dim(storminess)[3]))

# ============================================================================
# DEFINE REGIONS
# ============================================================================

regions <- list(
  list(
    name = "Fram Strait",
    abbr = "fram_strait",
    lon_range = c(-15, 15),
    lat_range = c(76, 82)
  ),
  list(
    name = "Svalbard-Barents",
    abbr = "svalbard_barents",
    lon_range = c(-10, 35),
    lat_range = c(74, 81)
  )
)

# ============================================================================
# LOOP THROUGH EACH REGION
# ============================================================================

for (region in regions) {
  
  region_name <- region$name
  region_abbr <- region$abbr
  
  cat("\n", rep("=", 80), "\n")
  cat(sprintf("PHASE 1 DIAGNOSTICS: %s REGION\n", toupper(region_name)))
  cat(rep("=", 80), "\n\n")
  
  # Define output directory

plot_dir <- here("Plots", "regional_diagnostics", region_abbr)
  if (!dir.exists(plot_dir)) dir.create(plot_dir, recursive = TRUE)
  
  # ==========================================================================
  # EXTRACT REGIONAL TIME SERIES
  # ==========================================================================
  
  cat("--- Extracting Regional Data ---\n")
  
  # Get indices for this region
  lon_sector_idx <- which(lon >= region$lon_range[1] & lon <= region$lon_range[2])
  lat_sector_idx <- which(lat >= region$lat_range[1] & lat <= region$lat_range[2])
  
  lon_sector_vals <- lon[lon_sector_idx]
  lat_sector_vals <- lat[lat_sector_idx]
  
  cat(sprintf("  Longitude range: %.1f° to %.1f° (%d grid cells)\n", 
              min(lon_sector_vals), max(lon_sector_vals), length(lon_sector_vals)))
  cat(sprintf("  Latitude range: %.1f°N to %.1f°N (%d grid cells)\n", 
              min(lat_sector_vals), max(lat_sector_vals), length(lat_sector_vals)))
  cat(sprintf("  Total grid cells: %d\n", 
              length(lon_sector_vals) * length(lat_sector_vals)))
  
  # Extract subset
  storminess_sector <- storminess[, lat_sector_idx, lon_sector_idx]
  
  # Create cosine-latitude weights
  weights_sector <- cos(lat_sector_vals * pi / 180)
  weights_matrix_sector <- matrix(weights_sector,
                                  nrow = length(lat_sector_vals),
                                  ncol = length(lon_sector_vals),
                                  byrow = FALSE)
  
  # Calculate area-weighted mean for each time step
  storm_ts_sector <- apply(storminess_sector, 1, function(slice) {
    weighted.mean(slice, weights_matrix_sector, na.rm = TRUE)
  })
  
  cat(sprintf("  ✓ Area-weighted time series created: %d months\n", length(storm_ts_sector)))
  
  # Aggregate to annual means
  monthly_df_sector <- data.frame(
    storminess = as.vector(storm_ts_sector),
    date = dates, 
    Year = year(dates)
  )
  
  annual_means_df_sector <- aggregate(storminess ~ Year, 
                                      data = monthly_df_sector, 
                                      FUN = mean)
  
  annual_ts_obj_sector <- ts(annual_means_df_sector$storminess, 
                             start = min(annual_means_df_sector$Year), 
                             frequency = 1)
  
  cat(sprintf("  ✓ Annual means created: %d years\n\n", length(annual_ts_obj_sector)))
  
  # ==========================================================================
  # PREPARE DATA FRAMES
  # ==========================================================================
  
  # Create monthly data frame
  regional_monthly_df <- data.frame(
    date = dates,
    storminess = as.vector(storm_ts_sector),
    year = year(dates),
    month = month(dates, label = TRUE, abbr = TRUE)
  )
  
  # Create annual data frame
  regional_annual_df <- data.frame(
    year = time(annual_ts_obj_sector),
    storminess = as.vector(annual_ts_obj_sector)
  )
  
  # ==========================================================================
  # PLOT 1: PRIMARY TIME SERIES VISUALIZATION
  # ==========================================================================
  
  cat("--- Creating Primary Time Series Plot ---\n")
  
  # Calculate statistics
  mean_val <- mean(regional_monthly_df$storminess, na.rm = TRUE)
  sd_val <- sd(regional_monthly_df$storminess, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  cat(sprintf("  Mean: %.2f m⁴/s⁴\n", mean_val))
  cat(sprintf("  SD: %.2f m⁴/s⁴\n", sd_val))
  
  # Calculate 12-month rolling mean
  regional_monthly_df <- regional_monthly_df %>%
    arrange(date) %>%
    mutate(rolling_12 = rollmean(storminess, k = 12, fill = NA, align = "center"))
  
  # Panel A: Monthly time series
  p1a <- ggplot(regional_monthly_df, aes(x = date, y = storminess)) +
    geom_line(aes(color = "Monthly values"), linewidth = 0.3, alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_line(aes(y = rolling_12, color = "12-month running mean"), 
              linewidth = 1.2, na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_hline(aes(yintercept = mean_val, 
                   linetype = sprintf("Long-term mean: %.1f m⁴ s⁻⁴", mean_val)), 
               linewidth = 0.7) +
    scale_color_manual(
      name = NULL,
      values = c("Monthly values" = "gray50", 
                 "12-month running mean" = "#D62728"),
      guide = guide_legend(order = 1)
    ) +
    scale_linetype_manual(
      name = NULL,
      values = c(setNames("dashed", sprintf("Long-term mean: %.1f m⁴ s⁻⁴", mean_val))),
      guide = guide_legend(order = 2)
    ) +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "10 years", date_labels = "%Y") +
    labs(
      title = "A. Monthly Time Series with 12-Month Running Mean",
      x = "Year",
      y = expression(paste("Storminess Index (m"^4, " s"^{-4}, ")"))
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#FFF9F0", color = NA),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
      legend.position = c(0.02, 0.98),
      legend.justification = c(0, 1),
      legend.background = element_blank(),
      legend.key = element_blank(),
      legend.key.width = unit(1.5, "cm"),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 9)
    )
  
  # Panel B: Annual means
  annual_mean <- mean(regional_annual_df$storminess)
  
  p1b <- ggplot(regional_annual_df, aes(x = year, y = storminess)) +
    geom_line(aes(color = "Annual means"), linewidth = 1.2) +
    geom_point(aes(color = "Annual means"), size = 2) +
    geom_hline(aes(yintercept = annual_mean, 
                   linetype = sprintf("Long-term mean: %.1f m⁴ s⁻⁴", annual_mean)), 
               linewidth = 0.7) +
    geom_smooth(aes(color = "Linear trend"), method = "lm", se = TRUE, 
                linewidth = 1, alpha = 0.2) +
    scale_color_manual(
      name = NULL,
      values = c("Annual means" = "#2CA02C", 
                 "Linear trend" = "#D62728"),
      guide = guide_legend(order = 1)
    ) +
    scale_linetype_manual(
      name = NULL,
      values = c(setNames("dashed", sprintf("Long-term mean: %.1f m⁴ s⁻⁴", annual_mean))),
      guide = guide_legend(order = 2)
    ) +
    labs(
      title = "B. Annual Mean Time Series",
      x = "Year",
      y = expression(paste("Annual Mean (m"^4, " s"^{-4}, ")"))
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#FFF9F0", color = NA),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
      legend.position = c(0.02, 0.98),
      legend.justification = c(0, 1),
      legend.background = element_blank(),
      legend.key = element_blank(),
      legend.key.width = unit(1.5, "cm"),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 9)
    )
  
  # Combine
  combined_ts <- p1a / p1b +
    plot_annotation(
      title = sprintf("%s: Storminess Index Time Series (1958–2024)", region_name),
      theme = theme(
        plot.title = element_text(size = 15, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)
      )
    )
  
  output_file_ts <- file.path(plot_dir, sprintf("Fig_%s_TimeSeries.png", region_abbr))
  ggsave(output_file_ts, combined_ts, width = 14, height = 10, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
  cat(sprintf("  ✓ Saved: %s\n", basename(output_file_ts)))
  
  # ==========================================================================
  # PLOT 2: ACF AND PACF ANALYSIS
  # ==========================================================================
  
  cat("\n--- Creating ACF/PACF Plot ---\n")
  
  max_lag <- 36
  acf_monthly <- acf(regional_monthly_df$storminess, lag.max = max_lag, plot = FALSE)
  pacf_monthly <- pacf(regional_monthly_df$storminess, lag.max = max_lag, plot = FALSE)
  
  n <- length(regional_monthly_df$storminess)
  ci_level <- 1.96 / sqrt(n)
  
  rho_1 <- acf_monthly$acf[2]
  
  rho_k <- acf_monthly$acf[-1][1:min(24, length(acf_monthly$acf[-1]))]
  k <- 1:length(rho_k)
  neff <- n / (1 + 2 * sum((1 - k/n) * rho_k))
  
  cat(sprintf("  Lag-1 autocorrelation (ρ₁): %.3f\n", rho_1))
  cat(sprintf("  Effective sample size: %.1f (%.1f%% of n=%d)\n", 
              neff, 100*neff/n, n))
  
  output_file_acf <- file.path(plot_dir, sprintf("Fig_%s_ACF_PACF.png", region_abbr))
  png(filename = output_file_acf, width = 12, height = 10, units = "in", res = 300, bg = "white")
  
  par(mfrow = c(2, 1),
      mar = c(4, 4.5, 3.5, 2),
      oma = c(2, 0, 3, 0),
      bg = "#FFF9F0")
  
  plot(acf_monthly, main = "", xlab = "Lag (months)", ylab = "Autocorrelation",
       las = 1, lwd = 2, ci.col = "#1F77B4", col = "gray30")
  mtext("A. Autocorrelation Function (ACF)", side = 3, line = 2.2, adj = 0, font = 2, cex = 1.1)
  mtext(bquote("Lag-1 autocorrelation: " * rho[1] * " = " * .(sprintf("%.3f", rho_1))),
        side = 3, line = 0.8, adj = 0, font = 1, cex = 0.9, col = "gray30")
  text(x = max_lag * 0.05, y = 0.95, labels = sprintf("95%% CI: ±%.3f", ci_level),
       pos = 4, col = "#1F77B4", font = 3, cex = 0.9)
  
  plot(pacf_monthly, main = "", xlab = "Lag (months)", ylab = "Partial Autocorrelation",
       las = 1, lwd = 2, ci.col = "#1F77B4", col = "gray30")
  mtext("B. Partial Autocorrelation Function (PACF)", side = 3, line = 2.2, adj = 0, font = 2, cex = 1.1)
  
  mtext(sprintf("Temporal Autocorrelation Structure: %s (1958–2024)", region_name),
        side = 3, line = 0.5, outer = TRUE, font = 2, cex = 1.3)
  mtext(bquote("n = " * .(n) * ", " * n[eff] * " = " * .(sprintf("%.0f", neff)) * 
               " (" * .(sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * (1 - neff/n))) * " reduction)"),
        side = 1, line = 0.5, outer = TRUE, font = 1, cex = 0.8, col = "gray40")
  
  dev.off()
  cat(sprintf("  ✓ Saved: %s\n", basename(output_file_acf)))
  
  # ==========================================================================
  # PLOT 3: DISTRIBUTION AND NORMALITY ASSESSMENT
  # ==========================================================================
  
  cat("\n--- Creating Distribution Assessment Plot ---\n")
  
  skewness <- (1/n) * sum((regional_monthly_df$storminess - mean_val)^3) / sd_val^3
  kurtosis <- (1/n) * sum((regional_monthly_df$storminess - mean_val)^4) / sd_val^4
  excess_kurtosis <- kurtosis - 3
  
  if (n <= 5000) {
    shapiro_test <- shapiro.test(regional_monthly_df$storminess)
  } else {
    shapiro_test <- shapiro.test(sample(regional_monthly_df$storminess, 5000))
  }
  
  cat(sprintf("  Skewness: %.3f\n", skewness))
  cat(sprintf("  Excess Kurtosis: %.3f\n", excess_kurtosis))
  cat(sprintf("  Shapiro-Wilk p-value: %.4f\n", shapiro_test$p.value))
  
  dist_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#FFF9F0", color = NA),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA)
    )
  
  p3a <- ggplot(regional_monthly_df, aes(x = storminess)) +
    geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 40, 
                   fill = "gray60", color = "gray30", alpha = 0.7) +
    stat_function(fun = dnorm, args = list(mean = mean_val, sd = sd_val),
                  color = "#D62728", linewidth = 1.2) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = mean_val, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
    labs(
      title = "A. Histogram with Normal Distribution",
      subtitle = sprintf("Skew = %.2f, Kurtosis = %.2f", skewness, excess_kurtosis),
      x = expression(paste("Storminess (m"^4, " s"^{-4}, ")")),
      y = "Density"
    ) +
    dist_theme
  
  theoretical_q <- qnorm(ppoints(n))
  sample_q <- sort(regional_monthly_df$storminess)
  qq_df <- data.frame(theoretical = theoretical_q, sample = sample_q)
  
  p3b <- ggplot(qq_df, aes(x = theoretical, y = sample)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 1, color = "gray40") +
    geom_abline(intercept = mean_val, slope = sd_val, color = "#D62728", linewidth = 1) +
    labs(
      title = "B. Q-Q Plot",
      subtitle = sprintf("Shapiro-Wilk p = %.4f", shapiro_test$p.value),
      x = "Theoretical Quantiles",
      y = "Sample Quantiles"
    ) +
    dist_theme
  
  regional_monthly_df <- regional_monthly_df %>%
    mutate(decade = paste0(floor(year / 10) * 10, "s"))
  
  p3c <- ggplot(regional_monthly_df, aes(x = decade, y = storminess)) +
    geom_boxplot(fill = "gray70", color = "gray30", alpha = 0.7,
                 outlier.color = "#D62728", outlier.size = 1.5) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = mean_val, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
    labs(
      title = "C. Distribution by Decade",
      x = "Decade",
      y = expression(paste("Storminess (m"^4, " s"^{-4}, ")"))
    ) +
    dist_theme +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
  
  regional_monthly_df <- regional_monthly_df %>%
    arrange(date) %>%
    mutate(rolling_sd = zoo::rollapply(storminess, width = 24, FUN = sd, 
                                        fill = NA, align = "center"))
  
  p3d <- ggplot(regional_monthly_df, aes(x = date, y = rolling_sd)) +
    geom_line(color = "#1F77B4", linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = sd_val, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "10 years", date_labels = "%Y") +
    labs(
      title = "D. Temporal Variability (24-month Rolling SD)",
      x = "Year",
      y = expression(paste("Rolling SD (m"^4, " s"^{-4}, ")"))
    ) +
    dist_theme +
    annotate("text", x = max(regional_monthly_df$date), y = sd_val,
             label = sprintf("Mean SD: %.1f", sd_val), hjust = 1.1, vjust = -0.5,
             size = 3, fontface = "italic")
  
  combined_dist <- (p3a | p3b) / (p3c | p3d) +
    plot_annotation(
      title = sprintf("Distribution Assessment: %s (1958–2024)", region_name),
      caption = sprintf("n = %d | Mean = %.1f | SD = %.1f", n, mean_val, sd_val),
      theme = theme(
        plot.title = element_text(size = 15, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
        plot.caption = element_text(size = 9, color = "gray40", hjust = 0.5)
      )
    )
  
  output_file_dist <- file.path(plot_dir, sprintf("Fig_%s_Distribution.png", region_abbr))
  ggsave(output_file_dist, combined_dist, width = 14, height = 11, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
  cat(sprintf("  ✓ Saved: %s\n", basename(output_file_dist)))
  
  # ==========================================================================
  # PLOT 4: MONTHLY CLIMATOLOGY
  # ==========================================================================
  
  cat("\n--- Creating Monthly Climatology Plot ---\n")
  
  monthly_clim <- regional_monthly_df %>%
    group_by(month) %>%
    summarise(
      mean = mean(storminess, na.rm = TRUE),
      sd = sd(storminess, na.rm = TRUE),
      se = sd / sqrt(n()),
      ci_lower = mean - 1.96 * se,
      ci_upper = mean + 1.96 * se,
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  peak_month <- monthly_clim$month[which.max(monthly_clim$mean)]
  peak_value <- max(monthly_clim$mean)
  trough_month <- monthly_clim$month[which.min(monthly_clim$mean)]
  trough_value <- min(monthly_clim$mean)
  annual_range <- peak_value - trough_value
  
  cat(sprintf("  Peak month: %s (%.1f m⁴/s⁴)\n", peak_month, peak_value))
  cat(sprintf("  Trough month: %s (%.1f m⁴/s⁴)\n", trough_month, trough_value))
  cat(sprintf("  Annual amplitude: %.1f m⁴/s⁴\n", annual_range))
  
  p4 <- ggplot(monthly_clim, aes(x = month, y = mean, group = 1)) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 0.5, xmax = 3.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
             fill = "#E3F2FD", alpha = 0.3) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 3.5, xmax = 6.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
             fill = "#F1F8E9", alpha = 0.3) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 6.5, xmax = 9.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
             fill = "#FFF9C4", alpha = 0.3) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 9.5, xmax = 12.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
             fill = "#FFE0B2", alpha = 0.3) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper), 
                  width = 0.3, color = "gray40", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_line(color = "#1F77B4", linewidth = 1.3) +
    geom_point(size = 4, color = "#1F77B4") +
    geom_point(data = subset(monthly_clim, month == peak_month),
               size = 5, color = "#D62728", shape = 17) +
    geom_point(data = subset(monthly_clim, month == trough_month),
               size = 5, color = "#2CA02C", shape = 17) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = mean_val, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
    labs(
      title = sprintf("Mean Annual Cycle: %s (1958–2024)", region_name),
      subtitle = sprintf("Peak: %s (%.0f) | Trough: %s (%.0f) | Amplitude: %.0f m⁴ s⁻⁴",
                        peak_month, peak_value, trough_month, trough_value, annual_range),
      x = "Month",
      y = expression(paste("Mean Storminess (m"^4, " s"^{-4}, ")"))
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, hjust = 0.5, color = "gray30"),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#FFF9F0", color = NA),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA)
    ) +
    annotate("text", x = 2, y = max(monthly_clim$ci_upper) * 1.05, label = "Winter", 
             size = 3.5, fontface = "italic", color = "#1565C0") +
    annotate("text", x = 5, y = max(monthly_clim$ci_upper) * 1.05, label = "Spring", 
             size = 3.5, fontface = "italic", color = "#558B2F") +
    annotate("text", x = 8, y = max(monthly_clim$ci_upper) * 1.05, label = "Summer", 
             size = 3.5, fontface = "italic", color = "#F9A825") +
    annotate("text", x = 11, y = max(monthly_clim$ci_upper) * 1.05, label = "Autumn", 
             size = 3.5, fontface = "italic", color = "#EF6C00") +
    annotate("text", x = which(monthly_clim$month == peak_month), 
             y = peak_value + annual_range * 0.08,
             label = "Peak", color = "#D62728", fontface = "bold", size = 4) +
    annotate("text", x = which(monthly_clim$month == trough_month), 
             y = trough_value - annual_range * 0.08,
             label = "Trough", color = "#2CA02C", fontface = "bold", size = 4) +
    annotate("text", x = 12.3, y = mean_val,
             label = sprintf("Annual mean: %.0f", mean_val),
             hjust = 1, vjust = -0.5, size = 3.5, fontface = "italic") +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.08, 0.12)))
  
  output_file_clim <- file.path(plot_dir, sprintf("Fig_%s_Climatology.png", region_abbr))
  ggsave(output_file_clim, p4, width = 14, height = 8, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
  cat(sprintf("  ✓ Saved: %s\n", basename(output_file_clim)))
  
  # ==========================================================================
  # PLOT 5: STL DECOMPOSITION
  # ==========================================================================
  
  cat("\n--- Creating STL Decomposition Plot ---\n")
  
  # Create time series object for STL
  storm_ts_obj <- ts(regional_monthly_df$storminess, 
                     start = c(1958, 1), 
                     frequency = 12)
  
  # Perform STL decomposition
  # t.window = 61 (~5 years) captures more decadal variability
  # s.window = "periodic" assumes constant seasonal pattern
  stl_result <- stl(storm_ts_obj, 
                    s.window = "periodic",
                    t.window = 61,  # ~5 years - captures more variability
                    robust = TRUE)
  
  # Extract components
  stl_df <- data.frame(
    date = regional_monthly_df$date,
    observed = as.vector(storm_ts_obj),
    trend = as.vector(stl_result$time.series[, "trend"]),
    seasonal = as.vector(stl_result$time.series[, "seasonal"]),
    remainder = as.vector(stl_result$time.series[, "remainder"])
  )
  
  # Calculate variance explained by each component
  var_total <- var(stl_df$observed, na.rm = TRUE)
  var_trend <- var(stl_df$trend, na.rm = TRUE)
  var_seasonal <- var(stl_df$seasonal, na.rm = TRUE)
  var_remainder <- var(stl_df$remainder, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  pct_trend <- 100 * var_trend / var_total
  pct_seasonal <- 100 * var_seasonal / var_total
  pct_remainder <- 100 * var_remainder / var_total
  
  # Calculate trend range for context
  trend_range <- max(stl_df$trend) - min(stl_df$trend)
  seasonal_range <- max(stl_df$seasonal) - min(stl_df$seasonal)
  
  cat(sprintf("  Variance explained:\n"))
  cat(sprintf("    Trend:     %.1f%% (range: %.1f m⁴/s⁴)\n", pct_trend, trend_range))
  cat(sprintf("    Seasonal:  %.1f%% (range: %.1f m⁴/s⁴)\n", pct_seasonal, seasonal_range))
  cat(sprintf("    Remainder: %.1f%%\n", pct_remainder))
  
  # Common theme for STL panels
  stl_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
      axis.title.x = element_blank(),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#FFF9F0", color = NA),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
      plot.margin = margin(5, 10, 5, 10)
    )
  
  # Panel 1: Observed data
  p_obs <- ggplot(stl_df, aes(x = date, y = observed)) +
    geom_line(color = "gray40", linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = mean_val, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "10 years", date_labels = "%Y") +
    labs(
      title = "A. Observed Data",
      y = expression(paste("m"^4, " s"^{-4}))
    ) +
    stl_theme
  
  # Panel 2: Trend component
  p_trend <- ggplot(stl_df, aes(x = date, y = trend)) +
    geom_line(color = "#D62728", linewidth = 1) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = mean_val, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "10 years", date_labels = "%Y") +
    labs(
      title = sprintf("B. Trend Component (%.1f%% of variance, range: %.0f m⁴ s⁻⁴)", 
                      pct_trend, trend_range),
      y = expression(paste("m"^4, " s"^{-4}))
    ) +
    stl_theme
  
  # Panel 3: Seasonal component
  p_seasonal <- ggplot(stl_df, aes(x = date, y = seasonal)) +
    geom_line(color = "#1F77B4", linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "10 years", date_labels = "%Y") +
    labs(
      title = sprintf("C. Seasonal Component (%.1f%% of variance, range: %.0f m⁴ s⁻⁴)", 
                      pct_seasonal, seasonal_range),
      y = expression(paste("m"^4, " s"^{-4}))
    ) +
    stl_theme
  
  # Panel 4: Remainder
  p_remainder <- ggplot(stl_df, aes(x = date, y = remainder)) +
    geom_line(color = "#2CA02C", linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "10 years", date_labels = "%Y") +
    labs(
      title = sprintf("D. Remainder (%.1f%% of variance)", pct_remainder),
      x = "Year",
      y = expression(paste("m"^4, " s"^{-4}))
    ) +
    stl_theme +
    theme(axis.title.x = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold", margin = margin(t = 10)))
  
  # Combine all panels
  combined_stl <- p_obs / p_trend / p_seasonal / p_remainder +
    plot_annotation(
      title = sprintf("STL Decomposition: %s Storminess Index (1958–2024)", region_name),
      subtitle = "Seasonal-Trend decomposition using LOESS | t.window = 61 months (~5 years)",
      theme = theme(
        plot.title = element_text(size = 15, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5, color = "gray30")
      )
    )
  
  output_file_stl <- file.path(plot_dir, sprintf("Fig_%s_STL_Decomposition.png", region_abbr))
  ggsave(output_file_stl, combined_stl, width = 14, height = 12, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
  cat(sprintf("  ✓ Saved: %s\n", basename(output_file_stl)))
  
  # ==========================================================================
  # REGION SUMMARY
  # ==========================================================================
  
  cat("\n", rep("-", 60), "\n")
  cat(sprintf("SUMMARY: %s\n", toupper(region_name)))
  cat(rep("-", 60), "\n")
  cat(sprintf("  Mean: %.2f m⁴/s⁴, SD: %.2f m⁴/s⁴\n", mean_val, sd_val))
  cat(sprintf("  ρ₁: %.3f, n_eff: %.0f (%.1f%% reduction)\n", rho_1, neff, 100*(1-neff/n)))
  cat(sprintf("  Peak: %s (%.0f), Trough: %s (%.0f)\n", 
              peak_month, peak_value, trough_month, trough_value))
  cat(sprintf("  Files saved to: %s\n", plot_dir))
  
}

# ============================================================================
# FINAL SUMMARY
# ============================================================================

cat("\n", rep("=", 80), "\n")
cat("ALL REGIONAL DIAGNOSTICS COMPLETE!\n")
cat(rep("=", 80), "\n\n")

cat("Output directories:\n")
for (region in regions) {
  cat(sprintf("  • %s: Plots/regional_diagnostics/%s/\n", 
              region$name, region$abbr))
}
cat("\n")
```

```{r mean-eke}
# ==============================================================================
# ANALYSIS OF MEAN EDDY KINETIC ENERGY (EKE) TRENDS (1958-2024)
# Purpose: Test if the average storm strength (amplitude) has changed.
# ==============================================================================

# --- 1. Load Data ---
# Adjust filename if necessary. This should be the MONTHLY MEAN EKE file.
eke_path <- here("Data_raw", "processed", "ERA5_EKE_monthly_raw.nc") 

if (!file.exists(eke_path)) {
  stop("File not found. Please check path.")
}

nc <- nc_open(eke_path)
eke_array <- ncvar_get(nc, "eke") # Expected dims: [lon, lat, time] or [time, lat, lon]
lat <- ncvar_get(nc, "latitude")
time <- ncvar_get(nc, "time")
nc_close(nc)

# Handle dimensions (Ensure [time, lat, lon])
# If dims are [lon, lat, time] (360, 35, 804), transpose:
if (dim(eke_array)[1] == 360) {
  eke_array <- aperm(eke_array, c(3, 2, 1))
}

# --- 2. Refine Domain (>= 60N) ---
lat_idx <- which(lat >= 60)
lat_arctic <- lat[lat_idx]
eke_arctic <- eke_array[, lat_idx, ] # [time, lat, lon]

# --- 3. Create Area-Weighted Time Series ---
# Weights based on cosine of latitude
weights <- cos(lat_arctic * pi / 180)
weights_mat <- matrix(weights, nrow = length(lat_arctic), ncol = dim(eke_arctic)[3], byrow = FALSE)

# Calculate spatial mean for each month
eke_ts_monthly <- apply(eke_arctic, 1, function(slice) {
  weighted.mean(slice, weights_mat, na.rm = TRUE)
})

# Create Dates
dates <- seq(as.Date("1958-01-15"), by = "month", length.out = 804)

# --- 4. Aggregate to ANNUAL Means ---
# Critical for trend analysis to remove seasonality
df_monthly <- data.frame(date = dates, eke = eke_ts_monthly, year = as.numeric(format(dates, "%Y")))
eke_ts_annual <- aggregate(eke ~ year, data = df_monthly, FUN = mean)
ts_vector <- eke_ts_annual$eke

# --- 5. Robust Trend Analysis ---

# A. Pre-Whitened Mann-Kendall (Significance)
acf_res <- acf(ts_vector, plot = FALSE)$acf[2]
cat(sprintf("Lag-1 Autocorrelation (Annual Mean EKE): %.3f\n", acf_res))

# Pre-whiten
n <- length(ts_vector)
ts_pw <- ts_vector[2:n] - acf_res * ts_vector[1:(n-1)]
mk_res <- mk.test(ts_pw)

# B. Sen's Slope (Magnitude)
sens <- sens.slope(ts_vector)
slope_decade <- sens$estimates * 10
baseline_mean <- mean(ts_vector[1:10]) # 1958-1967
total_change <- slope_decade * 6.7
pct_change <- (total_change / baseline_mean) * 100

# C. Bootstrap CI
boot_func <- function(data) {
  ts_boot <- ts(data, start = 1958, frequency = 1)
  sens.slope(ts_boot)$estimates
}
set.seed(123)
boot_res <- tsboot(ts_vector, boot_func, R = 5000, l = 3, sim = "fixed")
boot_ci <- boot.ci(boot_res, type = "perc")
ci_lower <- boot_ci$percent[4] * 10
ci_upper <- boot_ci$percent[5] * 10

# --- 6. Report Results ---
cat("\n=== RESULTS: MEAN EKE TREND (1958-2024) ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Baseline Mean: %.2f m2/s2\n", baseline_mean))
cat(sprintf("Sen's Slope: %.4f m2/s2 per decade\n", slope_decade))
cat(sprintf("Total Change: %.2f m2/s2 (%.1f%%)\n", total_change, pct_change))
cat(sprintf("P-Value (PW-MK): %.4f\n", mk_res$p.value))
cat(sprintf("95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n", ci_lower, ci_upper))

if (ci_lower < 0 && ci_upper > 0) {
  cat("CONCLUSION: No significant trend in Mean EKE.\n")
} else {
  cat("CONCLUSION: Significant trend detected.\n")
}

# --- 7. Plot ---
ggplot(eke_ts_annual, aes(x = year, y = eke)) +
  geom_line(color = "darkblue") +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red", se = FALSE, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Pan-Arctic Mean Eddy Kinetic Energy (1958-2024)",
       subtitle = "Annual Mean of 850 hPa EKE (>= 60N)",
       y = expression("EKE [m"^2*"/s"^2*"]"),
       x = "Year") +
  theme_bw()
```
